definition_zh: 块；团；肿块；把……归并；勉强接受
definition_en: a solid mass with no regular shape, a swelling on the body, to group separate things into one mass, or to accept something unpleasant because there is no other choice
core_image: 一块从煤堆里滚落的黑块，棱角不平，落在掌心沉甸甸的
scene: 厨房台面上放着一袋刚买回来的方糖，其中几块粘成了不规则的一团。He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea and watched it sink.
sceneCN: 这里 lump 是「块、团」（第 1 个义项：无定形的固体块）；句意为他往热茶里丢了一块方糖，看着它沉下去。图中可辨识物件：厨房台面、方糖袋、茶杯。

pos.zh: 块；团；肿块
把……归并；勉强接受

collocations.zh: 接受也得接受，不接受也得接受

derivatives.zh: 由 lump 加 -y 构成，义为「结块的；疙疙瘩瘩的」
由 lump 加 -ish 构成，义为「笨重的；迟钝的」

senses.title: A solid mass with no regular shape
senses.definition: a piece of solid material that has no regular shape and is felt as one heavy mass
senses.definitionCN: 一块没有规则形状、被感知为一整个沉重整体的固体
senses.example: He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他往热茶里丢了一块方糖。
senses.why: The word starts from what the hand feels: a portion of material that has set or been pressed into one body, with no edges worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从手的触感出发：一部分材料凝成或压成了一整块，边上没有值得去数的棱角。

senses.title: A swelling under the skin
senses.definition: an area of the body that has risen into a hard or rounded swelling
senses.definitionCN: 身体上隆起的一块硬或圆形的肿大部位
senses.example: She found a small lump on her arm and had it checked.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现手臂上有个小肿块，就去做了检查。
senses.why: A swelling has the same outline as a mass of clay or coal, so the body borrows the word for anything that pushes up under the skin.
senses.whyCN: 肿块与一团黏土或煤块的轮廓相同，于是身体借用了这个词，指任何在皮下顶起来的东西。

senses.title: To group things into one mass
senses.definition: to put separate people or things into one group without sorting them
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人或物不加区分地放进同一组
senses.example: The report lumps all the small shops together as one category.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把所有小店归并成同一类。
senses.why: If separate pieces are thrown into one pile, their edges disappear into a single mass; the verb is that throwing, applied to facts and categories.
senses.whyCN: 如果把分开的块丢进同一堆，它们的边就消失在一整团里；动词就是这一「丢」，只是对象换成了事实与类别。

senses.title: To accept something unpleasant
senses.definition: to swallow an unpleasant situation because it cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 因为无法改变而把不愉快的处境硬吞下去
senses.example: He did not like the decision, but he had to lump it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不喜欢这个决定，但也只能忍着接受。
senses.why: The phrase like it or lump it pictures the bad news as one hard lump that must be swallowed whole, since there is no way to chew it into smaller pieces.
senses.whyCN: like it or lump it 把坏消息想成一整块硬东西：既然没法嚼碎，就只能整块吞下。

intro.en: Lump is a Middle English noun for a shapeless mass; its deeper origin is uncertain, and the verb and medical senses grew from that solid block.
intro.cn: lump 是中古英语中表示「无定形一块」的名词；它更早的来源不确定，动词义与医学义都是从这块固体生长出来的。

items.en: The noun lump, also written lompe, first names a shapeless mass of material, neither shaped nor measured.
items.cn: 名词 lump 也写作 lompe，最初指一块既无形状也无定量的材料。

items.en: A common suggestion compares Middle Dutch lomp, a rag or a clumsy piece, and German Lumpen, a rag; the comparison is offered as possible, not as settled.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与中古荷兰语 lomp（破布、笨重的一块）和德语 Lumpen（破布）相比较；这只是一条可能的线索，并非定论。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense of throwing separate things into one mass, which gives phrases such as lump together and later lump sum.
items.cn: 动词义出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一整堆，由此产生 lump together 以及后来的 lump sum 等说法。

items.en: Medical writers use lump for a swelling felt under the skin, and the same outline produces the phrase a lump in the throat for strong emotion.
items.cn: 医学作者用 lump 指皮下摸到的肿块；同样的轮廓又产生 a lump in the throat 这一说法，用来形容情绪激动。

items.en: Phrases such as take one's lumps and like it or lump it keep the sense of a hard thing that simply has to be borne.
items.cn: take one's lumps 与 like it or lump it 之类的说法，保留了「一块硬东西只能硬扛」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and derivatives built on lump; the near-meaning group gathers words for masses, pieces and swellings.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lump 构成的变形与派生词；近义组收表示块状物、团块与肿起的词。

entries.definition: Full of lumps, or uneven in texture.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lump 加 -y 构成，义为「结块的；疙疙瘩瘩的」。

entries.definition: Heavy, awkward and slow in shape or manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lump 加 -ish 构成，义为「笨重的；迟钝的」。

entries.definition: More than one lump.
entries.definitionCN: lump 的复数形式，指多块。

entries.definition: One single payment of money instead of several.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lump 与 sum 复合，义为「一次性整付的总额」。

entries.definition: A thick, solid piece of something.
entries.definitionCN: 厚实的一块；多指从大块上切下的一块。

entries.definition: A solid piece with flat sides, often rectangular.
entries.definitionCN: 块；常指有平面、近似方形的固体。

entries.definition: A large amount of material with no clear shape.
entries.definitionCN: 一大团；强调整体而不强调边缘。

entries.definition: A place on the body that has become larger and rounder.
entries.definitionCN: 肿起；医学语境中比 lump 更中性的说法。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a shapeless mass, and its family keeps returning to hard pieces, swellings and things thrown into one pile.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一团无定形材料的名字，同族词反复回到硬块、肿起以及被丢成一堆的东西。

normal.en: Lump is first a noun for a shapeless mass; the verb comes later and means to throw separate things into one pile.
normal.cn: lump 首先是名词，指无定形的一团；动词义较晚出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一堆。

normal.en: Lump together keeps that picture: separate pieces lose their edges once they are dropped into the same heap.
normal.cn: lump together 保留了这个画面：分开的块一旦被丢进同一堆，就失去了各自的边。

normal.en: A lump of sugar is a small pressed block, which shows how loose the word is about exact shape.
normal.cn: 一块方糖就是压成的小方块，可见这个词对具体形状并不严格。

normal.en: A lump on the arm is a swelling shaped like a mass under the skin, so the medical sense borrows the physical one.
normal.cn: 手臂上的肿块就是皮下形似一团的东西，医学义直接借用了物理义。

normal.en: Like it or lump it means swallow the bad news whole, as if it were one hard lump with no way to chew it.
normal.cn: like it or lump it 意为把坏消息整块吞下，好像那是一块没法嚼的硬东西。

abstract.en: A lump has no edges to hold, which is why the word suits anything we cannot easily take apart.
abstract.cn: 一块 lump 没有可抓的棱角，所以这个词适合形容任何我们难以拆开的东西。

abstract.en: To lump people together is to lose the outlines that made them separate, and that is exactly the harm the verb describes.
abstract.cn: 把人 lump together，就是丢掉让他们彼此分开的轮廓，而这正是这个动词所指的害处。

abstract.en: A hard lump can be swallowed but not digested, which is a fair picture of a truth we accept without liking.
abstract.cn: 硬块吞得下却消化不了，这正好形容我们接受却并不喜欢的真相。

examples.cn: 他往热茶里丢了一块方糖。

examples.cn: 他不喜欢这个决定，但也只能忍着接受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隆噗」——一块东西落到桌面，闷闷一声；lump 就是块、团。

root: 中古英语 lump（也写作 lompe）指无定形的一块；来源不确定，一般认为可能与中古荷兰语 lomp（破布、笨重的一块）或德语 Lumpen（破布）有关，但没有定论，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one solid mass; the senses divide into the mass itself, the swelling on the body, the act of throwing things into a pile, and the act of swallowing an unpleasant thing whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一整块固体；义项由此分出块状物本身、身上的肿起、把东西丢成一堆的动作，以及把不快整块吞下的态度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black block rolling off a coal heap, its edges rough, heavy in the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块从煤堆里滚落的黑块，棱角不平，落在掌心沉甸甸的。

branches.cn: 从煤堆上滚落的一块黑煤

branches.en: a sugar cube dissolving at the bottom of a cup
branches.cn: 杯底慢慢化开的方糖

branches.en: a swelling rising under the skin
branches.cn: 皮肤下鼓起的一块肿

branches.en: odds and ends pushed into one pile
branches.cn: 零碎东西被推成一堆

branches.en: a man swallowing a bitter answer
branches.cn: 一个人把难堪的回答硬吞下去

intro.en: The word is a Middle English noun of uncertain origin; its English family is built with two suffixes and the ordinary verb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词是中古英语名词，来源不确定；它在英语里的同族词由两个后缀与常规动词形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Lump has no reliable Latin source; its origin is uncertain and is usually discussed through Dutch or German words, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: lump 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；它的来源不确定，通常在荷兰语或德语词里讨论，因此不列拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 月球的；月面的；按月亮计算的（阴历的）；与月亮有关的
definition_en: relating to the moon, or calculated by the moon's cycle rather than the sun's
core_image: 桌上摊开一本旧历，纸角画着月牙，红笔圈出按月亮排定的日子
scene: 桌上摊开一本旧历，纸页边角画着月牙，红笔圈出按月亮排定的节气。The old calendar on the desk marks its dates by a lunar cycle.
sceneCN: 这里 lunar 指「按月亮周期计算的」（第 3 个义项：阴历的、按月的）；句意为桌上那本旧历按月亮周期排定日期。图中可辨识物件：旧历、月牙图案、红笔圈记、桌面、窗光。

pos.zh: 月球的；月面的；阴历的；与月亮有关的

derivatives.zh: 精神失常的；疯子（旧时认为与月相有关）

senses.title: Of the moon
senses.definition: relating to the moon as a body, its position or its motion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为天体的月球、其位置或运动
senses.example: Lunar gravity is about one sixth of the earth's.
senses.exampleCN: 月球引力约为地球的六分之一。
senses.why: the adjective comes straight from the Latin noun for the moon, so it simply attaches 'moon' to another noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接来自拉丁语「月亮」名词，因此只是把「月亮」挂到另一个名词上。

senses.title: Of the moon's surface
senses.definition: used of the surface, soil, rocks and missions that reach the moon
senses.definitionCN: 指月球表面、月壤、月岩与抵达月球的探测活动
senses.example: The lunar dust clung to the astronauts' boots.
senses.exampleCN: 月尘粘在宇航员的靴子上。
senses.why: once spacecraft could land, the adjective shifted from the sky to the ground underfoot.
senses.whyCN: 当航天器能够着陆后，这个形容词便从天空转到了脚下的地面。

senses.title: Calculated by the moon
senses.definition: used of calendars and dates fixed by the moon's cycle rather than the sun's
senses.definitionCN: 指按月亮周期而非太阳周期确定的历法与日期
senses.example: The old calendar on the desk marks its dates by a lunar cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上那本旧历按月亮周期排定日期。
senses.why: a month was once counted by moons, so calendars that keep that reckoning are called lunar rather than solar.
senses.whyCN: 一个月曾按月亮计数，因此沿用这种算法的历法被称为 lunar，而非 solar。

senses.title: Phases and cycles
senses.definition: used of the moon's changing lit shape and the cycle it repeats
senses.definitionCN: 指月亮亮面形状的变化及其重复的周期
senses.example: Lunar phases repeat roughly every twenty-nine and a half days.
senses.exampleCN: 月相大约每二十九天半重复一次。
senses.why: the cycle is the moon's most regular behaviour, so the adjective often names time measured by that repetition.
senses.whyCN: 这一周期是月亮最规律的行为，因此这个形容词常命名按该重复计量的时间。

senses.title: The moon's pull on the sea
senses.definition: used of tides produced mainly by the moon's gravity
senses.definitionCN: 指主要由月球引力产生的潮汐
senses.example: The lunar tide is stronger than the sun's contribution.
senses.exampleCN: 月潮比太阳的贡献更强。
senses.why: the moon pulls the ocean more strongly than the distant sun, so tides are labelled by which body drives them.
senses.whyCN: 月球对海洋的牵引比遥远的太阳更强，因此潮汐按驱动它的天体来标记。

senses.title: Lunar orbit and bases
senses.definition: used of spacecraft paths around the moon and plans for structures on it
senses.definitionCN: 指绕月球的航天器路径以及在其上建造设施的规划
senses.example: The capsule entered lunar orbit on the third day.
senses.exampleCN: 太空舱在第三天进入月球轨道。
senses.why: space agencies needed to distinguish orbits at the moon from those at the earth, so 'lunar' became a routine prefix.
senses.whyCN: 航天机构需要区分月球轨道与地球轨道，于是 lunar 成了常用的前置限定词。

senses.title: Lunar deities and astrology
senses.definition: used of a god identified with the moon, or of astrological charts built on lunar positions
senses.definitionCN: 指与月亮等同的神，或依据月亮位置排出的星盘
senses.example: Roman writers described a lunar goddess with a crescent crown.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马作家描写过一位戴月牙冠的月亮女神。
senses.why: worship and astrology treat the moon as a power with a personality, keeping the adjective's oldest, personal use.
senses.whyCN: 崇拜与占星把月亮当作有人格的力量，保留了这个形容词最古老、人格化的用法。

senses.title: Lunar caustic
senses.titleCN: 旧医学术语：硝酸银（月牙剂）
senses.definition: in an old medical term, lunar caustic, silver nitrate used to burn away tissue
senses.definitionCN: 旧医学名词「月牙剂」，指用来烧灼组织的硝酸银
senses.example: Surgeons once used lunar caustic to close small wounds.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生曾用月牙剂来处理小伤口。
senses.why: alchemists marked silver with the moon's sign, so a silver compound carried 'lunar' into medicine.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术士用月亮符号标记银，于是含银的化合物把这个词带进了医学。

intro.en: Lunar comes from Latin lunaris 'of the moon', from luna 'moon'. Luna's own origin is often connected with a root meaning 'light', but that link is reconstructed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lunar 来自拉丁 lunaris「月亮的」，源头是 luna「月亮」。luna 自身的来源常被联系到一个意为「光」的词根，但这一联系属重构。年代均为约数。

items.en: Luna was both the moon and the moon goddess; like sol for the sun, one word served both roles.
items.cn: luna 既是月亮，也是月亮女神；如同 sol 之于太阳，一个词兼两职。

items.en: Many accounts derive luna from an older form meaning 'the shining one', related to lux 'light'; this is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 许多说法把 luna 追溯到意为「发光者」的更早形式，与 lux「光」相关；这是重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: The adjective lunaris 'of the moon' was formed with -alis, the suffix English later took as -al.
items.cn: 形容词 lunaris「月亮的」由 -alis 构成，英语后来把这个后缀借作 -al。

items.en: English borrowed lunar in the late Middle Ages, mostly in astronomy and medicine.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪末期借入 lunar，多用于天文学与医学。

items.en: English keeps native moon for the everyday object and Latin lunar for technical relations, a typical doublet.
items.cn: 英语用本族词 moon 指日常对象，用拉丁词 lunar 指技术关系，这是典型的同义双层词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between luna and the 'light' root is plausible but unproven, and any older Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：luna 与「光」词根的联系虽合理却未获证明，凡为其给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds Latin-derived words from the same luna stem; group two holds words describing moonlight and night.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 luna 词干的拉丁来源词；第二组是描述月光与夜晚的词。

entries.definition: The interval between two new moons; it turns the adjective's root into a measure of time.
entries.definitionCN: 两次新月之间的间隔；把词根变成时间量度。

entries.definition: Historically 'moon-struck', from the old belief that phases affected the mind; it is not a neutral medical word today.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上意为「被月亮击中的」，源于月相影响心智的旧信念；今天不是中性的医学词。

entries.definition: The pale half-moon at the base of a nail; a diminutive of luna, naming a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指甲根部淡色半月；是 luna 的指小形式，命名一种形状。

entries.definition: Situated beneath the moon, hence earthly and changeable in old cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 位于月亮之下，故在旧宇宙论中指尘世且可变的。

entries.definition: Reached by moonlight, as a moonlit path; it describes a result, not a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 被月光照到的，如月光下的小路；描述结果而非关系。

entries.definition: Active or occurring at night; lunar concerns the moon, not the whole night.
entries.definitionCN: 夜间活动或发生的；lunar 关乎月亮，而非整个夜晚。

entries.definition: Belonging to the sky in general; lunar is one narrow part of the celestial.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于天空；lunar 只是其中很窄的一部分。

entries.definition: The curved sickle shape of a young or old moon; it names a form rather than a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 新月或残月的弯曲镰形；命名形状而非关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin luna 'moon' + -aris: the technical adjective of the moon.
normal.cn: 拉丁 luna「月亮」+ -aris：月亮的技术形容词。

normal.en: English keeps both: moon for the object, lunar for the relation.
normal.cn: 英语两词并用：moon 指对象，lunar 指关系。

normal.en: Fixed terms: lunar surface, lunar landing, lunar calendar, lunar module.
normal.cn: 固定术语：月面、登月、阴历、登月舱。

normal.en: The family runs lunation, lunatic, lunula, sublunary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lunation、lunatic、lunula、sublunary。

normal.en: Alchemists marked silver with the moon, hence lunar caustic.
normal.cn: 炼金术士用月亮标记银，故有「月牙剂」之说。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar whose pages are cut in the shape of a crescent.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，纸页都剪成月牙形。

abstract.en: Picture a sea that rises because something far above is pulling it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海因为高处某物牵引而上涨。

abstract.en: Picture a silver coin stamped with a small moon.

examples.en: The lunar surface is covered with fine grey dust.
examples.cn: 月面覆盖着细灰的尘埃。

examples.en: The lunar calendar keeps the months aligned with the moon.
examples.cn: 阴历让月份与月亮保持一致。

examples.en: A lunar eclipse happens when the earth's shadow covers the moon.
examples.cn: 当地球的影子遮住月亮时，就发生月食。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the body to its surface, to the calendar it once set, to its phases, its tide, its orbits, its gods and finally a silver compound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从天体走到它的表面、它曾定下的历法、它的月相、它的潮汐、它的轨道、它的神祇，最后落到一种银化合物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crescent printed in the corner of an old calendar page.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧日历纸角上印着的一弯月牙。

branches.en: BODY AND GROUND: from the object in the sky to the dust underfoot.
branches.cn: 天体与地面：从天上对象到脚下尘土。

branches.en: TIME BY THE MOON: calendars and phases both count its cycle.
branches.cn: 按月计时：历法与月相都在数它的周期。

branches.en: PULL: the moon's gravity becomes a tide with its name.
branches.cn: 牵引：月球引力变成以它命名的潮。

branches.en: PATHS AND GODS: engineering orbits and old worship share the adjective.
branches.cn: 路径与神祇：工程轨道与古老崇拜共用这个形容词。

branches.en: ALCHEMY: silver was the moon's metal, so medicine kept the word.
branches.cn: 炼金术：银是月亮的金属，因此医学保留了这个词。

intro.en: Lunar is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective suffix; the root also forms several words through diminutive and prefix changes.
intro.cn: lunar 是拉丁名词加拉丁形容词后缀；同一词根还通过指小与前置成分构成若干词。

latinIntro.en: Latin luna and lunaris supply the core; lux 'light' is the root often proposed behind luna, though the link is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 luna 与 lunaris 提供核心；lux「光」是常被认为在 luna 背后的词根，但这一联系属重构。

definition_zh: 奢侈；奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；豪华的
definition_en: great comfort and expensive pleasure, a costly thing that is not necessary, a rare pleasure one allows oneself, or used before a noun for goods and places that are costly and high-grade
core_image: 橱窗里一只镶着金边的手袋，灯光把它照得像有温度
scene: 老城区的橱窗里摆着一只镶着金边的手袋，标价牌被灯光照得发亮。The shop window was filled with luxury goods that few people walking past could afford.
sceneCN: 这里 luxury 是「奢侈品」（第 2 个义项：并非必需而价格高昂的东西）；句意为橱窗里摆满了很少有人在路过时买得起的奢侈品。图中可辨识物件：老城区橱窗、镶金边的手袋、标价牌。

pos.zh: 奢侈；奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受
豪华的；高级的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 luxuri- 加 -ous 构成，义为「奢华的；豪华的」
由 luxurious 加 -ly 构成，义为「奢华地」
与 luxury 同一拉丁词干，义为「茂盛的；丰富的」，偏指生长繁密而非昂贵

senses.title: Great comfort and costly pleasure
senses.definition: a style of life full of expensive comfort and pleasure, more than plain need requires
senses.definitionCN: 充满昂贵舒适与享乐的生活方式，远超朴素的需要
senses.example: They lived in luxury after the business took off.
senses.exampleCN: 生意兴隆之后，他们过上了奢华的生活。
senses.why: Latin luxuria named excess and rank growth; the modern sense keeps that image of something spilling past the limit of what is needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 luxuria 本指过度与繁茂的生长；现代义保留了「漫过所需限度」这一意象。

senses.title: A costly thing that is not necessary
senses.definition: an expensive object or service bought for pleasure rather than for need
senses.definitionCN: 为享乐而非为需要购买的昂贵物品或服务
senses.example: The watch is a luxury, not a necessity.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是奢侈品，不是必需品。
senses.why: Once excess becomes a style of life, its objects can be counted one by one, so the abstract quality turns into things a person can own.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「过度」成为一种生活方式，它的物件就能一件件数出来，于是抽象的性质变成了可以拥有的具体东西。

senses.title: A rare pleasure one allows oneself
senses.titleCN: 难得的享受；小小的奢侈
senses.definition: something pleasant and not essential that a person allows themselves only now and then
senses.definitionCN: 令人愉快却并非必需、只偶尔允许自己享受的事物
senses.example: A long bath at the end of the week is a luxury.
senses.exampleCN: 周末结束时泡个长澡，是一种难得的享受。
senses.why: The word can shrink from a whole way of life to a single small indulgence, because the pleasure still costs more than ordinary routine would allow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从一整种生活方式缩小为一次小小的放纵，因为这份愉悦仍然比日常惯例所允许的更费钱费力。

senses.title: Costly and high-grade, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for goods, travel or housing that are expensive and meant to feel superior
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词之前，指昂贵且刻意营造高级感的商品、旅行或住宅
senses.example: They booked a luxury suite for the anniversary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为纪念日订了一间豪华套房。
senses.why: English often turns a noun of excess into a label placed before another noun, so the thing being sold carries the promise of the whole category.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示过度的名词变成放在另一名词前的标签，于是被出售的东西就带上了整个类别的承诺。

intro.en: Luxury comes from Latin luxus and luxuria, words for excess and profusion, which passed through Old French luxurie before English used it for costly comfort.
intro.cn: luxury 来自拉丁语 luxus 与 luxuria，意为过度与繁盛；它经古法语 luxurie 进入英语，后来才指昂贵的舒适。

items.en: Luxus names excess, extravagance and lavish display; a second Latin sense, a dislocation or displacement, is sometimes linked to it, but the relation between the two is debated.
items.cn: luxus 指过度、奢靡与铺张的展示；拉丁语中它另有一个「错位、脱节」的义项，有人把两者联系起来，但二者关系仍有争论。

items.en: Luxuria, built on luxus, means excess and profusion, and it also describes the rank, over-lush growth of plants.
items.cn: 由 luxus 构成的 luxuria 意为过度与繁盛，也用来描述植物疯长、过于茂密的生长。

items.en: Old French luxurie carries the word into English with a moral tone, meaning lust and dissolute living.
items.cn: 古法语 luxurie 带着道德评判把这词带进英语，意为淫欲与放荡的生活。

items.en: In Middle English luxurie is first a vice of excess, and only later does it drift towards costly comfort.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，luxurie 起初是一种过度放纵的恶习，后来才慢慢转向昂贵的舒适。

items.en: By the eighteenth century luxury has lost much of its moral sting, and in the twentieth century it also works as an adjective before nouns such as hotel and suite.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，luxury 的道德锋芒已大大减弱；到二十世纪，它还能作形容词放在 hotel、suite 这类名词之前。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin-stem family of adjectives and adverbs; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth, excess and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的形容词与副词；近义组收表示财富、过度与舒适的词。

entries.definition: Very comfortable and costly, as a room, a car or a life.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干构成的形容词，义为「奢华的；豪华的」。

entries.definition: In a costly and comfortable manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 luxurious 加 -ly 构成，义为「奢华地」。

entries.definition: Growing thickly and richly, used of hair, plants or style.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的形容词，义为「茂盛的；丰富的」，偏指生长繁密。

entries.definition: The quality of growing thickly or being richly abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的名词，义为「繁茂；丰盛」。

entries.definition: Great wealth shown openly in costly things and surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕；强调公开显示的财富与排场，比 luxury 更偏炫耀。

entries.definition: Spending more than is reasonable or necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 铺张；强调花费超出合理或必需，带批评色彩。

entries.definition: A pleasant state of ease without effort or pain.
entries.definitionCN: 舒适；只强调身心的安逸，不含昂贵之意。

entries.definition: Impressive and expensive beauty, especially of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 辉煌；强调视觉上的华美与气派，多用于场所。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin nouns for excess, and its family keeps returning to lavishness, growth beyond bounds and costly comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词上溯到表示过度的拉丁名词，同族词反复回到奢靡、越界生长与昂贵的舒适。

normal.en: Luxury goes back to Latin luxus, excess, so the word still carries the idea of more than need requires.
normal.cn: luxury 上溯到拉丁语 luxus（过度），所以这个词仍带着「超出所需」的意思。

normal.en: Latin luxuria also named the rank growth of plants, so lavishness and a plant spilling past its bounds share one picture.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 luxuria 也指植物疯长，所以铺张与植物漫出边界共享同一幅画面。

normal.en: Luxurious, luxuriant and luxury share one stem, but luxurious describes costly comfort while luxuriant describes thick growth.
normal.cn: luxurious、luxuriant 与 luxury 共用一个词干，但 luxurious 指昂贵的舒适，luxuriant 指茂密的生长。

normal.en: The French form luxurie came into English with a moral sting, meaning dissolute living before it meant fine things.
normal.cn: 法语形式 luxurie 带着道德批评进入英语，先指放荡的生活，后来才指精美的东西。

normal.en: In the lap of luxury is the fixed phrase for a life surrounded by costly comfort.
normal.cn: in the lap of luxury 是形容生活被昂贵舒适包围的固定说法。

abstract.en: A word born from excess suggests that luxury is defined not by objects but by the line they cross.
abstract.cn: 一个从「过度」中诞生的词说明，奢侈不由物品定义，而由它越过的界线定义。

abstract.en: The same root grows plants and sells suites, which is why richness always looks like something spilling over its edges.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根既让植物疯长，也用来卖套房，所以「丰盛」总像某种漫出边缘的东西。

abstract.en: Luxury is what comfort becomes when it stops answering a need and starts answering a desire.
abstract.cn: 奢侈就是舒适不再回应需要、转而回应欲望时的样子。

examples.en: The shop window was filled with luxury goods that few people walking past could afford.
examples.cn: 橱窗里摆满了很少有人在路过时买得起的奢侈品。

examples.en: They lived in luxury after the business took off.
examples.cn: 生意兴隆之后，他们过上了奢华的生活。

examples.en: They booked a luxury suite for the anniversary.
examples.cn: 他们为纪念日订了一间豪华套房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐奢瑞」——日子过得乐、又舍得奢，才叫 luxury；记住它是奢侈、奢华。

root: 拉丁语 luxus（过度、奢靡）与 luxuria（过量、繁茂的生长）经古法语 luxurie 进入英语；一般认为核心是「超出限度」，luxus 两义之间的关系学界仍有争论；luxurious、luxuriant 都从这一词干而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is excess beyond need; the senses divide into a lavish way of life, costly objects, a small rare indulgence, and the adjective for high-grade goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是超出所需的过度；义项由此分出奢华的生活方式、昂贵的物件、偶尔的小小放纵，以及指高级商品的形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold-trimmed handbag in a shop window, lit until it seems warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里一只镶着金边的手袋，灯光把它照得像有温度。

branches.en: a house kept far larger than the family needs
branches.cn: 一所远超家庭所需的房子

branches.en: a gold-trimmed bag behind lit glass
branches.cn: 灯光玻璃柜后镶金边的手袋

branches.en: a long bath taken without hurry
branches.cn: 不慌不忙泡的一个长澡

branches.en: a hotel door held open by a doorman
branches.cn: 门童替你拉开的酒店大门

branches.en: a price tag turned towards the light
branches.cn: 被转向灯光的标价牌

intro.en: The word is a Latin stem of excess with a French ending; its family adds the suffixes -ous and -ly to build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示过度的拉丁词干加上法语词尾；它的同族词加 -ous 与 -ly 构成形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Luxury has a recorded Latin family: luxus, luxuria and luxuriosus all belong to the same stem of excess and profusion.
latinIntro.cn: luxury 有可靠的拉丁同族词：luxus、luxuria 与 luxuriosus 都属于表示过度与繁盛的同一词干。

definition_zh: 机械；机器的总称；也指机构或运作体系
definition_en: machines taken as a group, or the working parts of a system, including an organisation's apparatus
core_image: 一排机器连着同一条传动轴，皮带一起转动，整片地面都在轻微震动
scene: 车间里一排机器连着同一条传动轴，皮带一齐转动，整片地面都在轻轻震动。The factory replaced its old machinery with one quieter line.
sceneCN: 这里 machinery 指机器的总称（第 1 个义项：成套机器）；句意：工厂把旧机械换成了一条更安静的产线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 机械（总称）；机器部件；机构

senses.title: Machines as a collective body
senses.definition: a group of machines considered together, especially in a workplace
senses.definitionCN: 被一并看待的一组机器，尤指工作场所中的
senses.example: The plant bought new machinery before hiring new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂先买新机械，再招新员工。
senses.why: the -ery ending makes a mass noun, so the word names machines as a body rather than one machine.
senses.whyCN: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，因此这个词指一批机器，而不是一台机器。

senses.title: The working parts inside a machine
senses.definition: the internal parts that transmit motion in a device
senses.definitionCN: 在装置内部传递运动的部件
senses.example: The clock's machinery needed oil, not a new face.
senses.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械部件需要上油，而不是换表盘。
senses.why: the collective noun also covers the parts that make one machine work, since they too are a set.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词也指使单台机器运转的那组部件，因为它们同样成组。

senses.title: The apparatus of an organisation
senses.definition: the people, offices and procedures that keep an institution running
senses.definitionCN: 维持一个机构运转的人员、部门与程序
senses.example: Reform stalled inside the machinery of the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 改革在部委的机构内部停住了。
senses.why: an organisation works through parts that transmit decisions, exactly as gears transmit motion.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠传递决定的部件运作，正如齿轮传递运动。

senses.title: A process treated as a system
senses.titleCN: 被当作系统看待的流程
senses.definition: the arrangeable steps by which something is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事时可加以安排的那些步骤
senses.example: The machinery of appeal is slow but predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 申诉的运作机制缓慢，却可预期。
senses.why: once steps are regular enough to be described, they can be spoken of as machinery.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤规律到可以被描述，人们就会把它说成机械装置。

senses.title: Farm equipment as a class
senses.definition: the tractors and implements used in farming, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的拖拉机与农具的总和
senses.example: Shared machinery let small farms afford a harvester.
senses.exampleCN: 共用机械让小农场也买得起收割机。
senses.why: the collective noun is the natural way to speak of a category of equipment bought and kept together.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词是谈论「成套购买与保管」的设备类别的自然方式。

senses.title: Stage and studio equipment
senses.definition: the rigging and devices that move scenery or sets
senses.definitionCN: 移动布景或场地的吊装与装置
senses.example: The theatre's machinery was hidden behind the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 剧院的舞台机械藏在幕布之后。
senses.why: theatre has used hidden devices for centuries, and the collective word names them without exposure.
senses.whyCN: 剧院使用隐蔽装置已有数百年，集合名词正好不必把它们露出来。

senses.title: The mechanism of an abstract force
senses.definition: the system by which a large process such as war or law is conducted
senses.definitionCN: 战争或法律等大型过程得以进行的系统
senses.example: The machinery of war outlived the government that built it.
senses.exampleCN: 战争的机器比建立它的政府活得更久。
senses.why: the figurative use extends to anything vast, impersonal and hard to stop.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法延伸到一切庞大、非人格且难以停止的事物。

senses.title: Heavy equipment on a site
senses.definition: the excavators and cranes that do the heavy physical work
senses.definitionCN: 从事繁重体力作业的挖掘机与起重机
senses.example: Heavy machinery arrived before the surveyors finished.
senses.exampleCN: 重型机械在测量员完工之前就进场了。
senses.why: on a site, the word means the class of large powered equipment, not a single tool.
senses.whyCN: 在工地上，这个词指大型动力设备这一类别，而不是单件工具。

intro.en: Machinery is a collective noun built on machine, which comes from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. The -ery ending turns one device into a body of devices.
intro.cn: machinery 是在 machine 上构成的集合名词，而 machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。-ery 词尾把一台装置变成一批装置。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a device, an engine of war or a means of doing something.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置、攻城器械或做事的手段。

items.en: Latin machina named a structure, scaffold or engine, and kept the Greek sense of a contrivance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，保留了希腊语「巧妙装置」的意思。

items.en: French machine carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, at first for any structure or device.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指任何结构或装置。

items.en: English machine narrowed toward powered devices as steam and industry spread.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与工业扩散，英语 machine 逐渐收窄为动力装置。

items.en: The ending -ery, from French -erie, gathers things into a mass or a trade, giving machinery, cutlery and stationery.
items.cn: 词尾 -ery 来自法语 -erie，把事物聚成整体或行业，形成 machinery、cutlery、stationery 这类词。

items.en: Bureaucracy and warfare gave the collective word its modern figurative sense of an impersonal working system.
items.cn: 官僚制度与战争给了这个集合词现代比喻义：非人格的运作系统。

note.en: The first group is the machine root in different shapes and counts; the second group is the neighbouring collective and system words.
note.cn: 第一组是「机器」词根的不同形态与单复数；第二组是相邻的集合与系统说法。

entries.definition: A single device; machinery is the mass of such devices, so it takes no plural.
entries.definitionCN: 指单台装置；machinery 是这类装置的整体，因此没有复数。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine; the collective noun names the equipment, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作机器的人；集合名词指设备，不指工人。

entries.definition: A particular arrangement of parts that produces motion; machinery is the wider set.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的某套部件组合；machinery 是更大的集合。

entries.definition: Of machines or done without thought; the noun machinery carries only the equipment sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的或不假思索的；名词 machinery 只保留设备义。

entries.definition: Any set of items needed for a purpose; machinery is specifically powered machines.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的所需的一整套物件；machinery 特指动力机器。

entries.definition: A set of parts working together for a function, often in science or politics.
entries.definitionCN: 为一功能共同运作的一整套部件，常用于科学或政治语境。

entries.definition: An organised set of parts or steps; machinery is the concrete or institutional version.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或步骤集合；machinery 是其具体或建制化的版本。

entries.definition: The buildings and machines of an industrial site taken as one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个工业场所的建筑与机器当作一个整体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real suffix and the real collective phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实词尾与真实集合搭配。

normal.en: The -ery ending makes a mass noun, as in cutlery and stationery.
normal.cn: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，如 cutlery、stationery。

normal.en: It takes no plural: one says much machinery, not many machineries.
normal.cn: 它没有复数：说 much machinery，而不说 many machineries。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: heavy machinery, agricultural machinery, industrial machinery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：重型机械、农业机械、工业机械。

normal.en: The figurative sense needs a system: the machinery of government, the machinery of justice.
normal.cn: 比喻义要接一个体系：政府机构、司法机制。

normal.en: One machine is a machine; a hall full of them is machinery.
normal.cn: 一台叫 a machine，一屋子就是 machinery。

abstract.en: Picture a single shaft running through a whole hall, so that every machine turns at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根轴穿过整个车间，于是所有机器同时转动。

abstract.en: Picture an office where decisions travel along belts nobody can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，决定沿着看不见的皮带传递。

abstract.en: Picture stage rigging moving a forest while the audience watches only the forest.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台吊装移动整片树林，而观众只看见树林。

examples.en: The mill's machinery was older than any of its workers.
examples.cn: 这家磨坊的机械比它的任何工人都老。

examples.en: Agricultural machinery changed the size of the average field.
examples.cn: 农业机械改变了普通田块的大小。

examples.en: Reform required changing the machinery, not just the minister.
examples.cn: 改革需要更换机构本身，而不只是换部长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）先（chine）瑞（ry）」——马先拉动的这一整套东西，就是机械

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置」→ 拉丁 machina → 法语 machine → 英语 machine；加集合词尾 -ery（法语 -erie）构成 machinery，指成套机器，后引申指机构与运作体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from machines as a body to the parts inside one, then to organisational apparatus, processes, farm equipment, stage rigging, abstract systems and site equipment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从成套机器出发，走向单台机器内部部件，再到组织机构、流程、农业装备、舞台吊装、抽象体系与工地设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of machines coupled to one shaft, belts turning together until the floor trembles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排机器接到同一根轴上，皮带一齐转动，地板微微发颤。

branches.en: EQUIPMENT CLASSES: machines in general, farm equipment, and heavy site plant.
branches.cn: 设备类别：泛指的机器、农业装备，以及工地重型设备。

branches.en: INNER PARTS: the set of parts that makes one device move.
branches.cn: 内部部件：使单台装置运动的那组零件。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL APPARATUS: offices, staff and procedures that keep an organisation running.
branches.cn: 机构装置：维持组织运转的部门、人员与程序。

branches.en: PROCESS AS SYSTEM: regular steps that can be described and rearranged.
branches.cn: 作为系统的流程：可被描述与重排的规律步骤。

branches.en: HIDDEN AND VAST: stage rigging behind a curtain, and the mechanism of war or law.
branches.cn: 隐蔽与庞大：幕后的舞台吊装，以及战争或法律的运作机制。

intro.en: Machinery is machine with a collective ending; the base itself came into English through French from Latin.
intro.cn: machinery 是 machine 加集合词尾；其词基本身经法语从拉丁语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of French machine; the collective ending -ery came separately through French -erie.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语 machine 的直接来源；集合词尾 -ery 另经法语 -erie 而来。

items.example: The Greek noun starts the chain of borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词开启了一连串借入。

items.example: Latin passed the word to French unchanged in sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语几乎原样把词义传给法语。

items.example: The base is a count noun and takes a plural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基是可数名词，有复数。

items.meaning: a body or trade of things
items.example: The ending gathers many machines into one mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把许多机器聚成一个整体。

items.example: The ending names the person who runs the equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指操作设备的人。

items.example: The ending builds the word for one assembly of parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「一套部件组合」的词。

items.example: The base appears across the whole technical family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基出现在整个技术词族中。

items.example: The ending produces the related adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾产生相关形容词。

latinEntries.structure: machina, machinae (n., first declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 宏观经济学；研究整体经济的产出、就业、物价与增长的经济学分支
definition_en: the branch of economics that studies the economy as a whole, especially total output, employment, price levels and growth
core_image: 一张从高空拍下的城市照片，港口、工厂与公路被压缩成几条并排的总量曲线
scene: 央行与财政部门的官员围坐一桌，争论的是全国产出、失业与物价的整体走向。Macroeconomics asks why total output and employment rise and fall together over the business cycle.
sceneCN: 央行与财政官员围坐一桌，争论全国产出、失业与物价的整体走向；句中的 macroeconomics 指「把整个经济当作一个总量单位来研究的分支」（第 1 个义项：研究整体经济运行的学科）。图中可辨识物件：总量曲线、城市航拍图、会议桌、报表。

pos.zh: 宏观经济学；总量经济学

derivatives.zh: 宏观经济的；总量经济的

senses.title: The branch studying the whole economy
senses.titleCN: 研究整体经济的学科分支
senses.definition: the division of economics that treats the economy as a single system rather than as separate markets
senses.definitionCN: 把经济当作一个单一体系、而非若干独立市场来研究的经济学分支
senses.example: Macroeconomics examines how investment and consumption move together.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学考察投资与消费如何同步变动。
senses.why: The prefix marks scale, and the base names the discipline, so the compound literally means the study of the economy at its largest scale.
senses.whyCN: 前缀标记尺度，基础词指学科，因此这个复合词字面上就是「在最大尺度上研究经济」。

senses.title: The university subject
senses.definition: the name of a standard course and textbook in a degree programme
senses.definitionCN: 学位课程中一门标准课程与教材的名称
senses.example: She took macroeconomics before moving on to monetary policy.
senses.exampleCN: 她先修宏观经济学，之后才转向货币政策。
senses.why: A discipline that is taught in set courses turns its branch names into subject titles, and this one is among the earliest in any programme.
senses.whyCN: 学科若按固定课程讲授，分支之名便成为科目名称，而这个分支是任何培养方案里最早的科目之一。

senses.title: The aggregate viewpoint
senses.definition: the habit of looking at totals and averages instead of at individual buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 看总量与平均值、而非单个买卖双方的习惯视角
senses.example: Macroeconomics smooths away individual choices to show the total picture.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学把个体选择抹平，以呈现总体图景。
senses.why: The word's scale prefix sets it against the small-scale branch, so using it signals that the unit of analysis is a total, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词表示尺度的前缀使它与小尺度分支相对，因此使用它就表明分析单位是总量而非个人。

senses.title: Analysis for fiscal and monetary policy
senses.titleCN: 为财政与货币政策服务的分析
senses.definition: the applied use of totals to decide on spending, taxation and interest rates
senses.definitionCN: 把总量分析用于决定支出、税收与利率的应用做法
senses.example: The treasury relied on macroeconomics to size the stimulus.
senses.exampleCN: 财政部依靠宏观经济学来确定刺激方案的规模。
senses.why: Governments act on totals, so the branch that supplies totals became the natural language of budget and rate decisions.
senses.whyCN: 政府依据总量行动，因此提供总量的分支自然成为预算与利率决策的语言。

senses.title: Short-run fluctuation
senses.definition: the study of booms and recessions over months and a few years
senses.definitionCN: 研究数月到数年之间的繁荣与衰退
senses.example: Macroeconomics explains why recessions spread from one sector to all.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学解释衰退为何从一个部门扩散到所有部门。
senses.why: When totals are measured quarterly, their short swings become visible, and the branch took that rhythm as one of its central problems.
senses.whyCN: 总量一旦按季度计量，短期摆动便显现出来，这个分支便把这种节奏当作核心问题之一。

senses.title: Long-run growth
senses.definition: the study of why output per person rises over decades
senses.definitionCN: 研究数十年间人均产出为何提高
senses.example: Macroeconomics now devotes much of its attention to productivity growth.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学如今把大量注意力放在生产率增长上。
senses.why: The same totals, viewed across decades rather than quarters, raise the separate question of growth, which the branch treats as its long horizon.
senses.whyCN: 同样一些总量若按数十年而非季度来看，便提出增长这一独立问题，这个分支把它当作长期视野。

senses.title: The open economy
senses.titleCN: 开放经济中的宏观分析
senses.definition: the study of totals when trade, exchange rates and capital cross borders
senses.definitionCN: 在贸易、汇率与资本跨越国界时研究总量
senses.example: Macroeconomics of the open economy tracks the trade balance alongside growth.
senses.exampleCN: 开放经济的宏观经济学把贸易差额与增长一并追踪。
senses.why: Once national totals are measured against other countries, the branch must add exchange rates and cross-border flows to its core accounts.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国民总量要与他国比较，这个分支就必须在核心核算中加入汇率与跨境流动。

senses.title: Loose talk about the big picture
senses.titleCN: 口语引申：从整体层面看问题
senses.definition: in informal use, the habit of judging a local event by its effect on the whole system
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指以整体体系所受影响来判断局部事件的习惯
senses.example: Treating the plant closure as macroeconomics, the mayor asked what it did to the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 市长把工厂关闭当作宏观层面的问题，追问它给整个城镇带来了什么。
senses.why: Because the term's core is the whole rather than the part, it can be borrowed for any decision that must be judged at the level of the system.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个术语的核心是整体而非局部，它可以被借用来描述任何必须在体系层面判断的决定。

intro.en: Macroeconomics joins a Greek prefix meaning 'long, large' to economics, which descends from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia. The compound and its adjective are generally thought to have risen in the 1930s with national income accounting and Keynesian aggregate analysis; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个表示「长的、大的」的希腊前缀加在经济学科之名上，而后者经拉丁 oeconomia 源自希腊 oikonomia。一般认为这个复合词及其形容词形式在二十世纪三十年代随国民收入核算与凯恩斯式总量分析兴起；具体首见年份来源不确定。

items.en: Makros meant 'long, large, far-reaching' and was widely used in compounds for things on a great scale.
items.cn: makros 意为「长的、大的、范围广的」，广泛用于表示大尺度的复合词。

items.en: Oikonomia, from oikos 'household' and nemein 'to manage', named the running of a household and later of public affairs.
items.cn: oikonomia 由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「管理」构成，指经营家宅，后也指管理公共事务。

items.en: Latin oeconomia carried the word into European learned usage, where it covered the management of an estate or a state.
items.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 把这个词带入欧洲学术用语，其范围包括庄园或国家的管理。

items.en: In the nineteenth century political economy was shortened to economics, giving the base that the large-scale prefix would later attach to.
items.cn: 十九世纪政治经济学缩称为经济学，为后来加接大尺度前缀提供了基础词。

items.en: The adjective is generally thought to have appeared in the 1930s, when economists needed a word for analysis of totals rather than of single markets.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词在二十世纪三十年代出现，当时经济学家需要为「分析总量而非单个市场」造一个词。

items.en: The noun settled as the name of a branch in the same decade, alongside national income accounts and aggregate demand analysis; the first recorded year is uncertain.
items.cn: 同一时期，这个名词固定为一个分支的名称，与国民收入核算和总需求分析相伴；最早见于记载的年份不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms from the same compound that differ in word class or scale; the near-meaning group holds neighbouring fields that also work with totals but answer different questions.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一复合词中词性或尺度不同的形式；近义组收的是同样处理总量、但回答不同问题的邻近领域。

entries.definition: Describes totals or the branch itself, as in macroeconomic policy; it cannot stand alone as the name of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 描述总量或该分支本身，如宏观经济政策；它不能单独用作课程名称。

entries.definition: Studies single buyers, sellers and markets; the two words share their ending and are constantly paired and confused.
entries.definitionCN: 研究单个买方、卖方与市场；两词词尾相同，常被成对使用也常被混淆。

entries.definition: The whole subject, of which the large-scale branch is one part; it is broader, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 整个学科，大尺度分支只是其中一部分；它范围更广，并非同义词。

entries.definition: Names the whole economy as an object; it is what the branch studies, not the study itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为研究对象的整体经济；它是该分支研究的对象，而不是研究本身。

entries.definition: The measurement of total output, income and spending; it supplies the data that the branch interprets.
entries.definitionCN: 对总产出、总收入与总支出的计量；它提供该分支所解读的数据。

entries.definition: A narrower study of expansions and contractions; it is one part of the larger branch, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 对扩张与收缩的更窄研究；它是该分支的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: Studies money, banking and interest rates; it overlaps with the branch but centres on one mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究货币、银行与利率；它与该分支重叠，却以一个机制为中心。

entries.definition: Explains why output per person rises over decades; it is the long-run wing of the branch.
entries.definitionCN: 解释数十年间人均产出为何提高；它是该分支的长期一翼。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here use the real Greek scale prefix, the real household root behind economics, and the real institutional setting in which the term grew up.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自表示尺度的真实希腊前缀、经济学背后真实的治家词根，以及这个术语成长的真实制度背景。

normal.en: Makros means long or large, so the prefix marks the scale of the whole economy.
normal.cn: makros 意为长或大，因此这个前缀标记的是整个经济的尺度。

normal.en: Oikonomia, household management, is the same root that gave economics.
normal.cn: oikonomia 即治家之术，正是给经济学提供词根的那个词。

normal.en: The field grew with national income accounting, which first made totals measurable.
normal.cn: 这门分支随国民收入核算成长，后者第一次让总量可以被计量。

normal.en: The pair with microeconomics is built into the word: large scale against small scale.
normal.cn: 它与微观经济学的配对就写在这个词里：大尺度对小尺度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the teaching sense: intermediate macroeconomics, applied macroeconomics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出教学义：中级宏观经济学、应用宏观经济学。

abstract.en: Picture an aerial photograph in which a whole city becomes a few clean lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张航拍照片，整座城市被压缩成几条干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture three curves, output, jobs and prices, drawn on one board and read together.
abstract.cn: 想象一块板子上画着产出、就业与物价三条曲线，被一起解读。

abstract.en: Picture one lever in a control room that is said to move every household at once.
abstract.cn: 想象控制室里的一根拉杆，据说能同时牵动每一个家庭。

examples.en: Macroeconomics is usually taught after students have learned how single markets work.
examples.cn: 宏观经济学通常在学生了解单个市场如何运行之后才讲授。

examples.en: The central bank's forecasts are grounded in macroeconomics rather than in firm-level data.
examples.cn: 央行的预测依据的是宏观经济学，而不是企业层面的数据。

examples.en: A recession is the kind of event that macroeconomics was invented to explain.
examples.cn: 衰退正是宏观经济学被创立出来要解释的那类事件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「麦克罗伊科诺米克斯」：麦克罗先生只翻全国的厚账本，看的是整体的大数，不是一家小店的流水。

root: 希腊 makros「长的、大的」+ 希腊 oikonomia（oikos「家宅」+ nemein「管理」）→ 拉丁 oeconomia → 英语中的经济学；再加表示「大」的前缀构成宏观经济学，一般认为二十世纪三十年代随国民收入核算与总量分析定型，首见年份来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: the branch is named, taught, defined by its aggregate viewpoint, applied to policy, divided into short swings and long growth, widened to open economies, and finally borrowed in speech for any whole-system view.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：先给分支命名，再进入课堂，以总量视角界定自身，用于政策，分为短期波动与长期增长，扩展到开放经济，最后被口语借去指任何整体层面的看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one dashboard where the whole country's output, jobs and prices are read as a single instrument.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块仪表盘，全国的产出、就业与物价被当作同一台仪器来读。

branches.en: NAMING AND TEACHING: the branch is defined by its whole-economy object, then fixed as a standard course and textbook.
branches.cn: 命名与教学：该分支以整体经济为对象而被界定，随后固定为标准课程与教材。

branches.en: VIEWPOINT AND USE: looking at totals rather than individuals, and turning those totals into budget and rate decisions.
branches.cn: 视角与用途：看总量而非个体，再把总量变成预算与利率决策。

branches.en: TIME SCALES: quarterly swings of boom and slump, and the decades-long rise of output per person.
branches.cn: 时间尺度：季度性的繁荣与衰退摆动，以及数十年的人均产出增长。

branches.en: BORDERS: exchange rates, trade balances and capital flows enter the same accounts.
branches.cn: 国界：汇率、贸易差额与资本流动进入同一套核算。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the term escapes the classroom and names any judgment made at the level of the whole.
branches.cn: 被借用的尺度：这个术语走出课堂，用来指任何在整体层面作出的判断。

intro.en: The word is a prefix plus a discipline noun: a Greek element of size in front, and the household-derived name of economics behind.
intro.cn: 这个词是「前缀加学科名词」：前面是表示尺度的希腊成分，后面是由治家一词演变来的经济学之名。

latinIntro.en: Latin oeconomia and oeconomicus provide the older European forms of the economics half, while the size element was latinised as a combining form.

senses.title: Supernatural power used to change events
senses.definition: the supposed power to make things happen by charms, spells or secret forces beyond nature
senses.definitionCN: 通过咒语、符咒或超自然隐秘力量左右事物的、被认为存在的能力
senses.example: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。
senses.why: Greek magos named a Persian priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became the ordinary word for power over events that nature does not explain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 magos 指波斯的占星祭司，这类祭司的技艺后来成了「支配自然无法解释之事的力量」的日常说法。

senses.title: Conjuring tricks performed on stage
senses.definition: the art of producing baffling effects by sleight of hand, hidden props and misdirection
senses.definitionCN: 依靠手上功夫、暗藏道具与转移注意，制造出令人困惑效果的行当
senses.example: Her act mixed quick card magic with a dove that vanished from a hat.
senses.exampleCN: 她的节目把快速的纸牌魔术和一只从帽子里消失的鸽子混在一起。
senses.why: A stage performer copies the effects the old craft claimed, so the same noun now names a trick that everyone knows is a trick.
senses.whyCN: 舞台艺人复制了古老技艺号称能做到的效果，于是同一个名词如今指一场人人都知道是假的戏法。

senses.title: A compelling, unexplained charm
senses.definition: a quality in a place, person or moment that seems to work on people beyond ordinary cause
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某人或某一刻身上那种仿佛超出常理、能打动人的特质
senses.example: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。
senses.why: If magic means power that acts without visible cause, then a place that moves people without explanation can simply be said to have magic in it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 magic 指没有可见原因就起作用的力量，那么一个说不清为何打动人的地方，自然就可以说身上带着魔力。

senses.title: Wonderful and enchanting, as an adjective
senses.definition: used beside a noun for something that seems to work beyond ordinary means or feels enchanting
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词旁边，形容某物仿佛以超乎常理的方式奏效，或令人觉得着迷
senses.example: The garden looked magic under the first snow of winter.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下时，那座园子看起来像被施了魔法。
senses.why: Once the noun names a power that changes things, placing it beside another noun turns it into a plain adjective for the effect.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词指一种改变事物的力量，把它放到另一个名词旁边，就自然变成了描述那种效果的形容词。

intro.en: Magic is a word borrowed from the title of a foreign priesthood; it then split into a claimed supernatural art, a harmless stage act, a felt charm and a plain adjective.
intro.cn: magic 是从一个外来祭司称号借来的词；它后来分成号称的超自然技艺、人畜无害的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及一个普通形容词。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old Persian maguš, a member of a priestly class who read the stars and performed rites.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追到古波斯语 maguš，指主持仪式、观测星象的祭司阶层成员。

items.en: Greek adopted the title as magos for a Persian priest or a wandering wise man, and the abstract craft was called magikē.
items.cn: 希腊语把这个称号借作 magos，指波斯祭司或游走的智者，而那种抽象的技艺被称为 magikē。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as magicus, and the related noun named the art itself rather than the man.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 magicus，相关的名词则指那门技艺本身，而不是那个人。

items.en: Old French magique carried noun and adjective into medieval Europe, and English borrowed the forms in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 magique 把名词与形容词一起带进中世纪的欧洲，英语在十三、十四世纪借入这些形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps magic for the occult art and for the stage act, adds the figurative charm, and uses the bare noun before other nouns as an adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 magic 指神秘技艺与舞台表演，加上比喻性的魅力，并把光秃秃的名词放在其他名词前当形容词用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and the biblical plural of the priestly title; the near group gathers other words for magic arts and for tricks of the senses.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词与那个祭司称号的圣经复数；近义组收其他表示法术以及感官幻象的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the title of a foreign priest, and its family keeps returning to hidden knowledge, stage deception and the charm that needs no explanation.

normal.en: Latin magicus and Old French magique carried the word to English, which shortened the ending to magic.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magicus 与古法语 magique 把词带到英语，英语把词尾缩短成 magic。

normal.en: Magician adds -ian to name the person, magical adds -al for the quality, and magically adds -ly for the manner.
normal.cn: magician 加 -ian 指人，magical 加 -al 指性质，magically 再加 -ly 指方式。

normal.en: A magic wand and a magic trick keep the stage sense, while black magic keeps the darker ritual sense.
normal.cn: magic wand 与 magic trick 守住舞台义，black magic 守住了更阴暗的仪式义。

normal.en: The adjective use grew by putting the noun before another noun, as in a magic spell or a magic touch.

abstract.en: Magic survives because people still want a short name for effects they cannot explain.

abstract.en: The same word covers a trick you can learn and a power you can only imagine.
