definition_zh: 岩浆；地下熔融岩石；岩浆房；岩浆类型（玄武质、花岗质）；行星岩浆洋；泛指熔融物质；比喻压抑的强烈情绪或力量
definition_en: molten rock stored beneath the surface of a planet, which may cool to form igneous rock or reach the surface as lava
core_image: 地表之下极深处，一汪橙红的黏稠熔体在岩壁间缓慢翻滚，被上方厚重的岩层死死压住
scene: 钻探船的甲板上，仪器显示地下深处有一层缓慢流动的高温熔体，压力正在上升。 Scientists drill into the ocean floor to sample the magma before it reaches the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 magma 指仍在地下的熔融岩石（第 1 个义项：位于地表之下、尚未喷出的熔融态岩石）；句意为科学家钻入海底，在岩浆到达地表之前取样。

pos.zh: 岩浆；地下熔融岩石
岩浆体（如岩浆房、岩浆洋）
泛指熔融物质；比喻压抑的强烈情绪或力量

derivatives.zh: 岩浆的；与岩浆作用有关的
岩浆学（较少见的学科名称）
岩浆房（复合术语，指储存岩浆的地下腔体）
岩浆洋（复合术语，指行星早期的全球性熔融层）

senses.title: Molten rock underground
senses.definition: molten or partly molten rock stored beneath the surface of a planet
senses.definitionCN: 储存于行星地表之下、呈熔融或半熔融状态的岩石
senses.example: The magma rose slowly through a network of cracks.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆沿着裂隙网络缓慢上升。
senses.why: Greek magma meant a kneaded mass; geologists applied it to rock softened by heat into a paste-like body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 magma 意为「揉成的团块」；地质学家用它指被热软化成糊状团块的岩石。

senses.title: A chamber that stores magma
senses.definition: a large body of magma held within the crust, often feeding a volcano
senses.definitionCN: 地壳中储存大量岩浆的腔体，常为火山提供补给
senses.example: Seismic surveys revealed a magma chamber three kilometres below the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 地震勘测显示峰顶下方三公里处有一个岩浆房。
senses.why: the mass had to be located somewhere, so the container sense grew out of the material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这团熔体总得存在于某处，于是「容器」义从「材料」义中生长出来。

senses.title: Magma typed by composition
senses.titleCN: 按成分划分的岩浆类型
senses.definition: a melt described by its chemical composition, such as basaltic or granitic magma
senses.definitionCN: 按化学成分描述的熔体，如玄武质岩浆或花岗质岩浆
senses.example: Basaltic magma is hotter and runnier than granitic melt.
senses.exampleCN: 玄武质岩浆比花岗质熔体更热、更稀。
senses.why: composition decides how a melt behaves, so the word came to name varieties rather than one substance.
senses.whyCN: 成分决定熔体的行为，因此这个词开始指称不同品种，而非单一物质。

senses.title: Any molten material
senses.definition: a general term for a hot melt, including molten metal, glass or ice
senses.definitionCN: 对高温熔体的泛称，包括熔融金属、玻璃或冰
senses.example: The furnace stirred a magma of molten glass and ash.
senses.exampleCN: 炉中翻搅着一团熔融玻璃与灰的混合物。
senses.why: the paste image is broad enough to cover industrial and planetary melts that are not rock.
senses.whyCN: 「糊状团块」的意象足够宽，可覆盖并非岩石的工业熔体与行星熔体。

senses.title: A planet-wide magma ocean
senses.definition: a global layer of molten rock on a young planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 年轻行星或卫星上全球性的熔融岩石层
senses.example: The early Moon probably had a magma ocean hundreds of kilometres deep.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的月球可能有一层深达数百公里的岩浆洋。
senses.why: planetary science extended the underground body to the whole surface of a young world.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学把地下的熔体扩展到年轻天体的整个表面。

senses.title: Mixing of two magmas
senses.definition: the process in which two different magmas meet and blend, often before an eruption
senses.definitionCN: 两种不同岩浆相遇并混合的过程，常发生在喷发之前
senses.example: Textures in the lava record magma mixing just before the blast.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩中的结构记录了爆发前一刻的岩浆混合。
senses.why: the word works as an attributive noun here, so the compound can name a process between two bodies of melt.
senses.whyCN: 在这个复合术语中该词作定语名词，因此整个复合词能指两团熔体之间的过程。

senses.title: The parent magma
senses.definition: the original melt from which a series of related rocks or melts are derived
senses.definitionCN: 一系列相关岩石或熔体所由衍生的原始熔体
senses.example: Geochemists traced all the samples back to one parental magma.
senses.exampleCN: 地球化学家把全部样品追溯至同一个母岩浆。
senses.why: the word works as a family term, with melts descending from a common source as children from a parent.
senses.whyCN: 该词被当作家族术语：各熔体如同子女，源自同一个母体。

senses.title: Suppressed fury like magma
senses.definition: a figurative use for strong feeling or power that is held down and may break out
senses.definitionCN: 比喻被压住、可能冲破而出的强烈情绪或力量
senses.example: Resentment had been gathering like magma beneath the quiet office.
senses.exampleCN: 怨气像岩浆一样在那间安静的办公室里积攒。
senses.why: magma is invisible and dangerous precisely because it is still under the crust, which makes it a natural image for held-in anger.
senses.whyCN: 岩浆之所以危险，正因为它仍在壳下、看不见，这使它成为压抑怒气的天然意象。

intro.en: Magma comes from Greek magma, a kneaded mass, from massein, to knead. Latin used magma only as a Greek loanword, so there is no native Latin family behind it. Geology adopted the term in the nineteenth century for molten rock still underground, specifically to contrast with lava at the surface.
intro.cn: magma 一般认为源自希腊 magma「揉成的团块」，出自动词 massein「揉、捏」，但更早的前希腊词根并不确定。拉丁语中的 magma 只是希腊借词，背后没有本土拉丁词族。地质学在十九世纪采用该词指仍在地下的熔融岩石，特意与已到地表的 lava 相对。

items.en: Massein meant to knead, press or work a soft substance with the hands.
items.cn: massein 意为「揉、压」，用手把柔软之物反复捏合。

items.en: Magma was the result: a kneaded mass, and in medical Greek a thick ointment or paste.
items.cn: magma 是结果：揉成的一团；在希腊医学中还指浓稠的药膏或糊剂。

items.en: Latin texts used magma as an unassimilated Greek word. It has no Latin verb or noun relatives, which is why this entry leaves the Latin list empty.
items.cn: 拉丁文献把 magma 当作未同化的希腊词使用。它没有拉丁动词或名词同族，因此本词条的拉丁词表留空。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology needed a word for melt that had not yet reached the surface; magma filled that gap.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学需要一个词指尚未到达地表的熔体，magma 正好补上这个空位。

items.en: The word now covers magma chambers, magma oceans, magma mixing and parental magma, and is also used figuratively.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖岩浆房、岩浆洋、岩浆混合与母岩浆，也被用于比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (root in doubt): the Greek origin is generally accepted, from magma, a kneaded mass, and massein, to knead; but the deeper pre-Greek root of massein is unsettled, any older form offered for it is a reconstruction, and the exact date of the geological sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：一般认为是希腊 magma「揉成的团块」，出自 massein「揉、捏」，这一路径获较广泛接受；但 massein 更早的前希腊词根并无定论，凡给出的更深形式均属重构形式，地质义的确切首见年代亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same word; group two holds the terms most often confused with magma.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一个词构成的形式；第二组是最容易与岩浆混淆的术语。

entries.definition: Relating to magma or to the processes that involve it, as in magmatic water or magmatic differentiation.
entries.definitionCN: 与岩浆或岩浆参与的过程有关，如岩浆水、岩浆分异。

entries.definition: The total activity of magma within a region, including its generation, movement and solidification.
entries.definitionCN: 一个区域内岩浆活动的总和，包括生成、运移与固结。

entries.definition: An uncommon plural modelled on Greek and Latin neuter plurals; magmas is the usual form.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿希腊语与拉丁语中性复数构成的少见复数；常用复数仍是 magmas。

entries.definition: The underground reservoir that holds magma; the phrase names the container, not the melt.
entries.definitionCN: 储存岩浆的地下储库；这个短语指容器，而非熔体本身。

entries.definition: The same molten rock once it has reached the surface; magma is the underground stage, lava the exposed stage.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种熔融岩石到达地表之后的名称；magma 是地下阶段，lava 是露出地表的阶段。

entries.definition: A plain description of rock heated until liquid; magma is the technical term for it underground.
entries.definitionCN: 对加热至液态的岩石的平实描述；magma 是它在地下时的术语。

entries.definition: In petrology, a synonym for liquid rock or the liquid portion of a partly molten system.
entries.definitionCN: 在岩石学中指液态岩石，或部分熔融体系中的液相部分。

entries.definition: Describing rock formed from cooled magma or lava; it names the product, not the molten stage.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由冷却的岩浆或熔岩形成的岩石；指产物，而非熔融阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphology, real collocations and the real magma-lava boundary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊构词、真实搭配，以及真实存在的岩浆与熔岩分界。

normal.en: Greek massein means to knead: magma is rock softened and worked into a glowing paste.
normal.cn: 希腊 massein 意为「揉」：岩浆就是被揉软、揉成一团的灼热糊状岩石。

normal.en: Magma stays below, lava comes out: one word for the hidden stage, one for the exposed stage.
normal.cn: 岩浆留在地下，熔岩流到地表：一个词指隐藏阶段，一个词指露出阶段。

normal.en: Compound terms come in a series: magma chamber, magma ocean, magma mixing, parental magma.
normal.cn: 复合术语成串出现：岩浆房、岩浆洋、岩浆混合、母岩浆。

normal.en: Composition splits it into basaltic magma and granitic magma, the first hotter and runnier.
normal.cn: 按成分可分为玄武质岩浆与花岗质岩浆，前者更热、更稀。

normal.en: The figurative use keeps the position: anger sits under the surface like magma under crust.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留了位置：怒气伏在表面之下，如同壳下的岩浆。

abstract.en: Picture dough being folded and pressed in a bowl until it becomes one soft mass.
abstract.cn: 想象面团在盆里被反复折叠按压，最后成了一团柔软的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a thick soup held down by a lid, steam bubbling only at the rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅浓汤被盖子压住，热气只在边缘冒出细泡。

abstract.en: Picture a hidden underground river that makes the ground above slightly warm.
abstract.cn: 想象地下有一条看不见的暗河，让上方的地面微微发烫。

examples.en: The magma cooled slowly at depth, forming coarse crystals.
examples.cn: 岩浆在深处缓慢冷却，形成粗大的晶体。

examples.en: A magma chamber beneath the caldera was detected by seismic waves.
examples.cn: 地震波探测到破火山口下方有一个岩浆房。

examples.en: Her anger sat like magma, unseen until the day it broke through.
examples.cn: 她的怒气像岩浆一样伏着，直到爆发那天才被看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 希腊语「揉成的团」——地热把岩石揉软，还压在地壳里 → 岩浆

root: 希腊 magma「揉成的团块」，出自 massein「揉、捏」；拉丁语仅作希腊借词使用，无本土同族；地质学借指地下熔融岩石，与地表的 lava（熔岩）分工。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hidden body: a kneaded melt that sits under rock. The material sense comes first, then its container, its composition, the wider class of melts, planetary and process uses, a source term, and finally the figurative pressure it suggests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个隐藏的物体：一团伏在岩石之下的熔体。先讲物质本身，再讲容器、成分、更宽的熔体类别、行星与过程用法、源熔体，最后落在它暗示的压抑之势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kneaded, glowing paste trapped under a lid of rock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团被岩石盖子压住的灼热糊状物。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND CONTAINER: the melt itself, and the cavity that holds it.
branches.cn: 物质与容器：熔体本身，以及容纳它的腔体。

branches.en: COMPOSITION AND SOURCE: chemistry sorts the melt into types, and one type can be the parent of a rock series.
branches.cn: 成分与来源：化学把熔体分成类型，而某一类型可以成为一套岩石系列的母体。

branches.en: BEYOND ROCK: the same paste image covers industrial melts and a planet-wide molten layer.
branches.cn: 越出岩石：同一个糊状意象覆盖工业熔体与全球性的熔融层。

branches.en: PROCESS BETWEEN BODIES: two melts can meet and blend before an eruption.
branches.cn: 两团之间的过程：两股熔体可以在喷发前相遇并混合。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE PRESSURE: what is held under the crust becomes the image of held-in fury.
branches.cn: 比喻压力：压在壳下之物，成为被压抑怒气的意象。

intro.en: Magma is not built from Latin prefixes and suffixes; it is a whole Greek noun borrowed intact, so these items are stems and compounds rather than derivational endings.
intro.cn: magma 不是由拉丁前缀与后缀构成的，而是整体借入的希腊名词；因此下列条目是词干与复合形式，而非派生词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes no native relatives: magma appears only as a Greek loanword, and the geological vocabulary is built by compounding with English and Latin elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有提供本土同族词：magma 只作为希腊借词出现，地质词汇靠英语与拉丁成分复合构成。

items.example: The stem magma- appears unchanged in English.
items.exampleCN: 词干 magma- 在英语中保持原形。

items.example: Magmatic describes anything that belongs to magma.
items.exampleCN: magmatic 描述一切属于岩浆的事物。

items.structure: -ismos (Greek noun suffix of activity or system)
items.example: Magmatism names the activity of magma in a region.
items.exampleCN: magmatism 指一个区域内的岩浆活动。

items.example: Magmatology is the study of magmas and their evolution.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆学是研究岩浆及其演化的学问。

items.example: The chamber fed the eruption for several weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这个岩浆房为喷发供给了数周。

items.example: The magma ocean solidified from the top down.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆洋自上而下固结。

items.example: Magma mixing can trigger an eruption.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆混合可能触发喷发。

items.meaning: source melt of a rock series
items.meaningCN: 一套岩石系列的源熔体
items.example: The parental magma was rich in magnesium.
items.exampleCN: 母岩浆富含镁。

items.meaning: change of melt composition by crystal separation
items.meaningCN: 熔体成分因晶体分离而改变
items.example: Magmatic differentiation produces different rock types.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆分异产生不同的岩石类型。

items.example: Basaltic magma feeds quiet lava flows.
items.exampleCN: 玄武质岩浆供给平静的熔岩流。

definition_zh: 磁铁；磁石；有吸引力的人或地方
definition_en: an object that attracts iron and produces a magnetic field, or a person or place that draws others
core_image: 一块黑亮的石头压在铁钉堆上，钉子像树枝一样从它身上长出来
scene: 厨房里，孩子把一张画纸吸在冰箱门上，纸没有掉下来，门上还挂着一串回形针。A small magnet holds the drawing while the fridge door swings open.
sceneCN: 这里 magnet 指「能吸铁的磁体」（第 2 个义项：人造的小块磁铁）；句意为一块小磁铁吸住画纸，冰箱门打开时纸也没掉。图中可辨识物件：冰箱门、画纸、彩色磁贴、回形针；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 磁铁；磁体；磁石
有吸引力的人；吸引人群的地方

derivatives.zh: 磁的；有磁性的；有吸引力的

senses.title: The natural stone
senses.definition: a piece of naturally magnetized iron ore that attracts iron
senses.definitionCN: 天然带磁性的铁矿石，能吸铁
senses.example: The old compass held a sliver of magnet cut from native ore.
senses.exampleCN: 那只旧罗盘里装着一小片从天然矿石上切下来的磁石。
senses.why: Before manufacture, the word meant the ore itself: a stone found already able to move iron.
senses.whyCN: 在人工制造出现之前，这个词指的就是矿石本身：一块被发现时就已经能移动铁的石头。

senses.title: A shaped piece of magnetized metal
senses.titleCN: 人造磁铁：加工成形的磁体
senses.definition: a piece of metal or ceramic made so that it attracts iron
senses.definitionCN: 经过加工、能吸铁的金属或陶瓷块
senses.example: He stuck the note to the fridge with a small magnet.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一块小磁铁把便条贴在冰箱上。
senses.why: The same power found in ore can be shaped into bars and discs, so the noun widened from a found stone to a made tool.
senses.whyCN: 矿石里的那种力量可以被加工成条块与圆片，于是这个名词从捡到的石头扩大到做出来的工具。

senses.title: A coil with an iron core
senses.titleCN: 电磁铁：靠电流工作的磁体
senses.definition: a coil of wire with an iron core that acts as a magnet while current flows
senses.definitionCN: 通电时起磁体作用的带铁芯线圈
senses.example: The crane's magnet releases the scrap metal when the current stops.
senses.exampleCN: 电流一断，吊车的电磁铁就把废金属放开。
senses.why: Once electricity could make magnetism, a magnet no longer had to be a permanent stone; it could be switched on and off.
senses.whyCN: 当电能够制造磁性，磁体就不必再是永久的石头，而可以被开与关。

senses.title: The two poles of a magnet
senses.definition: one of the two ends of a magnet, where the pull is strongest and opposite poles attract
senses.definitionCN: 磁体两端吸力最强之处，异极相吸、同极相斥
senses.example: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, however often it is cut.
senses.exampleCN: 无论把磁铁切多少次，每一块都仍有南极和北极。
senses.why: The object is not uniform: the pull concentrates at the ends, and that pair of ends is part of what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 物体并不均匀：吸力集中在两端，而这一对端点也是这个词所指内容的一部分。

senses.title: A charming person
senses.definition: a person who attracts others strongly, as if by magnetism
senses.definitionCN: 像被磁力吸引那样强烈吸引他人的人
senses.example: As a speaker she was a magnet, and the hall filled within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 作为演讲者，她像一块磁石，几分钟就把礼堂填满了。
senses.why: A stone that draws iron is an easy picture for a person who draws a crowd, so the noun moved from metal to people.
senses.whyCN: 吸铁的石头很容易拿来比喻吸住人群的人，于是这个名词从金属转到了人。

senses.title: A place that draws visitors
senses.definition: a place that attracts many visitors or residents
senses.definitionCN: 吸引大量游客或居民的地方
senses.example: The rebuilt pier became a magnet for day trippers.
senses.exampleCN: 重建后的码头成了当日游客的聚集地。
senses.why: A place pulls people the way the stone pulls iron: no one orders the crowd to come, yet the current of visitors bends toward it.
senses.whyCN: 地方吸人就像磁石吸铁：没有人下令，游客的人流却朝它弯过去。

senses.title: A centre that draws resources
senses.titleCN: 吸引人才与资金的中心
senses.definition: an institution or district that draws talent, money or investment
senses.definitionCN: 吸引人才、资金或投资的机构或地区
senses.example: The research park is a magnet for young engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座研究园区是年轻工程师的聚集地。
senses.why: The metaphor turns practical: a place that offers work and equipment draws skilled people and their money as reliably as a field draws iron.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转为实用：一个提供工作与设备的地方，吸来技术人才与资金，其可靠程度如同磁场吸铁。

senses.title: Anything that captures attention
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：吸引注意力的事物
senses.definition: anything that holds attention so firmly that people turn to it
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住注意力、让人转向它的事物
senses.example: That question acted as a magnet for the whole debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题像磁石一样吸住了整场辩论。
senses.why: The pull can attach to nothing physical at all: an idea holds attention the way a stone holds filings, and the noun needs no metal.
senses.whyCN: 这种拉力完全可以不附着在任何实物上：一个念头抓住注意，就像石头抓住铁屑，这个名词不再需要金属。

intro.en: Magnet comes from the Greek name of the stone of Magnesia through Latin and Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnet 经拉丁语与古法语，上溯希腊语中「马格尼西亚的石头」之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos, the stone of Magnesia, named a natural iron ore that already attracted iron. The place-name account is generally accepted; the origin of the place name is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 即「马格尼西亚的石头」，指一种本身就能吸铁的天然矿石。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的；地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and used it for the ore and for anything that behaved like it.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该希腊名词作 magnes，属格 magnetis，既指矿石，也指任何行为像它的东西。

items.en: Old French magnete carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, at first as the name of the mineral.
items.cn: 古法语 magnete 在十三世纪把这个词带进英语，最初是矿物的名字。

items.en: Experimenters began shaping iron into artificial magnets, and the word widened from a found stone to any made object with the same power.
items.cn: 实验者开始把铁加工成人造磁体，这个词也从「捡到的石头」扩大到任何具有同样力量的制成品。

items.en: In 1825 William Sturgeon wrapped a coil around an iron core and called it an electromagnet, tying the noun to a switchable device.
items.cn: 1825 年斯特金把线圈绕在铁芯上，称之为电磁铁，把这个名词与可开关的装置绑在一起。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries a magnet was also a person or place that draws others, especially visitors, talent or money.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，magnet 也指吸引他人的人或地方，尤其吸引游客、人才或资金。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stem and one look-alike from another root; group two holds things that attract in the same practical way.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词干的词，以及一个异源形近词；第二组是在实际用途上同样能吸引东西的事物。

entries.definition: Describes what a magnet is or does; the noun names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 形容磁体是什么、能做什么；名词则指物件。

entries.definition: The property or the science; a magnet is the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 性质或学科；magnet 是拥有这一性质的东西。

entries.definition: The black mineral that magnets are made from and that occurs naturally magnetized.
entries.definitionCN: 可用来制作磁体、也会天然带磁的黑色矿物。

entries.definition: A business magnate, from Latin magnus 'great'; it is not related to the stone at all.
entries.definitionCN: 商业巨头，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；与磁石毫无同源关系。

entries.definition: The old name for naturally magnetized magnetite, the original magnet.
entries.definitionCN: 天然带磁的磁铁矿的旧称，也就是最早的磁石。

entries.definition: A magnet that works only while current flows, so it can be turned off.
entries.definitionCN: 只在通电时起作用的磁体，因此可以关掉。

entries.definition: Any drawing force; a magnet is one physical source of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何拉力；磁体是它在物理上的一种来源。

entries.definition: The act of pulling a crowd or interest; a magnet is the object that produces the draw.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人群或兴趣的动作；magnet 是产生这种吸引的物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stone name, the real compounds and the real modern metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的石名、真实的复合词，以及真实存在的现代比喻。

normal.en: The word is the stone, not the property: magnet names the thing, magnetism names what it has.
normal.cn: 这个词指的是石头而非性质：magnet 指物件，magnetism 指它拥有的东西。

normal.en: Everyday magnets carry prefixes: electromagnet, nanomagnet, fridge magnet.
normal.cn: 日常磁体常带前缀：电磁铁、纳米磁体、冰箱贴。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the figurative sense: a magnet for tourists, a magnet for talent, a magnet school.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示比喻义：吸引游客的地方、吸引人才的中心、特色择优学校。

normal.en: The same stone name gives magnetite, the ore, and magnetometer, the measuring device.
normal.cn: 同一个石名还给出 magnetite（矿石）与 magnetometer（测量器械）。

normal.en: Cut a magnet in half and you do not get one pole; you get two smaller magnets, each with both poles.
normal.cn: 把磁铁切成两半，你不会得到一个单极，而是得到两块更小的磁铁，各有两极。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that grows iron branches when it is laid on a pile of nails.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头放在钉堆上，就长出铁的枝条。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that turns attraction on and off without moving the metal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关，不动金属就能让吸引力出现或消失。

abstract.en: Picture a town where every road seems to slope gently toward the same square.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇，每条路都像微微向下倾向同一个广场。

examples.en: A magnet is useless once it is heated far above its working temperature.
examples.cn: 磁铁被加热到远超工作温度之后就没用了。

examples.en: The festival has become a magnet for young filmmakers.
examples.cn: 这个影展已经成了年轻电影人的聚集地。

examples.en: She kept the spare key under a magnet on the steel door.
examples.cn: 她把备用钥匙放在钢门上的磁贴下面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 马格内特——来自马格尼西亚的石头，能吸铁 → 磁石、磁铁

root: 希腊 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚石）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 古法语 magnete → 英语 magnet。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the native ore and the shaped object, then its poles and its electric version, and end with the person, place and idea that draw others.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从天然矿石与成形磁体出发，经过两极与电磁版本，最后落到吸人的人、地方与念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black stone with iron nails growing out of it like branches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黑石头上长出铁钉，像树枝一样。

branches.en: Found stone and made object: the same power, first in ore and then in a shaped piece.
branches.cn: 捡来的石头与制成的物件：同一种力量，先在矿石里，后在成形块里。

branches.en: A magnet can be switched by current, and every version still has two poles.
branches.cn: 磁体可由电流开关，而无论哪种版本都仍有两极。

branches.en: The stone's pull applied to a person who holds a room.
branches.cn: 磁石的拉力用在一个人身上，他能稳住一屋子人。

branches.en: A place or an institution that pulls visitors, talent and money.
branches.cn: 一个地方或机构，吸来游客、人才与资金。

branches.en: The pull detached from place and metal, working on attention itself.
branches.cn: 拉力脱离地方与金属，直接作用于注意力。

intro.en: Magnet is a free noun from Greek through Latin, and all its relatives attach ordinary suffixes to that stem.
intro.cn: magnet 是经拉丁语来自希腊语的自由名词，所有亲属词都在这同一词干上加普通后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes, genitive magnetis, is the direct source; magnetismus is a New Latin extension, and Greek magnēs stands at the head of the chain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes（属格 magnetis）是直接来源；magnetismus 是新拉丁语的延伸，链条最前端是希腊 magnēs。

items.example: The magnet clung to the steel frame.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁吸在钢架上。

items.meaning: having the power of a magnet
items.meaningCN: 有磁性的（加形容词后缀，物件转为性质）
items.example: The magnetic clamp held the plate.
items.exampleCN: 磁性夹具固定住板块。

items.meaningCN: 磁性（加状态后缀，物件转为性质）
items.example: Magnetism faded as the metal cooled.
items.exampleCN: 金属冷却后磁性减弱。

items.meaning: to make an object act like a magnet
items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加使动后缀，性质被赋予别的物件）
items.example: A brief pulse magnetizes the needle.
items.exampleCN: 一次短脉冲就能使指针磁化。

items.meaning: the process or strength of being magnetized
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化强度（再加过程后缀）
items.example: The magnetization survived the drop.
items.exampleCN: 跌落之后磁化状态仍在。

items.meaning: the black ore that magnets occur in
items.meaningCN: 磁铁矿（加矿物后缀，由物件转为矿种）
items.example: Magnetite grains darken the sand.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁矿颗粒把沙子染黑。

items.meaning: a magnet driven by a coil
items.meaningCN: 电磁铁（电加磁体，动力来源变成电流）
items.example: The electromagnet lifts the car bodies.
items.exampleCN: 电磁铁把车身吊起。

items.meaning: a small decorative magnet for a refrigerator
items.meaningCN: 冰箱贴（由冰箱与磁体复合，用途收窄到装饰）
items.example: She bought a fridge magnet at the museum.
items.exampleCN: 她在博物馆买了一个冰箱贴。

latinEntries.meaning: the region behind the stone's name

definition_zh: 有磁性的；磁的；靠磁力驱动的；有强烈吸引力的
definition_en: having the power to attract iron, or relating to magnets, magnetic fields and the force they produce
core_image: 一块黑色矿石隔着白纸把铁屑排成一道道弧线，纸下什么都没有，铁屑却自己排队
scene: 实验室的白纸上，一块黑色矿石压着薄薄一层铁屑，铁屑自己排成弧线，围观的人都屏住了呼吸。A magnetic mineral draws iron filings into curved lines even through a sheet of paper.
sceneCN: 这里 magnetic 指「具有吸引铁、能产生磁场的性质」（第 1 个义项：能够吸引铁并形成磁场）；句意为一块有磁性的矿石隔着白纸也能把铁屑吸成弧线。图中可辨识物件：黑色矿石、白纸、铁屑、放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有磁性的；磁的；靠磁力工作的
有魅力的；有强烈吸引力的

senses.title: Attracting iron
senses.definition: having the property of attracting iron and producing a magnetic field around itself
senses.definitionCN: 具有吸引铁并在周围产生磁场的性质
senses.example: A magnetic rod lifted every nail from the bench in one sweep.
senses.exampleCN: 一根有磁性的棒子一扫，就把工作台上的钉子全吸了起来。
senses.why: The word names the property that first made a certain ore famous: iron moves toward it although nothing visible pulls.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是让某种矿石最早出名的性质：看不见任何东西在拉，铁却朝它移动。

senses.title: Belonging to the study of magnets
senses.titleCN: 与磁学、磁力研究有关的
senses.definition: relating to magnetism as a subject of scientific study
senses.definitionCN: 与作为科学研究对象的磁学、磁力有关
senses.example: Her thesis examines the magnetic behaviour of thin films.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文研究薄膜的磁性行为。
senses.why: Once the stone became an object of experiment, the adjective shifted from the object to the whole field of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 当磁石成为实验对象之后，这个形容词就从物件本身转到了整个研究领域。

senses.title: Driven by magnetic force
senses.definition: operated or produced by magnetic forces rather than by direct contact
senses.definitionCN: 靠磁力而非直接接触来运转或产生
senses.example: The magnetic levitation train floats above its guideway.
senses.exampleCN: 磁悬浮列车悬浮在导轨上方。
senses.why: If a stone can move iron without touching it, that pull can also be harnessed to lift a whole train.
senses.whyCN: 既然磁石不接触就能移动铁，这股拉力自然也就能用来托起整列火车。

senses.title: Of a planet's field
senses.definition: relating to the natural field generated by a planet or a star
senses.definitionCN: 与行星或恒星自然产生的磁场有关
senses.example: Migrating birds appear to read the magnetic field of the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙的鸟似乎能读取地球的磁场。
senses.why: The same invisible influence surrounds the whole planet, so the adjective applies to fields far larger than any stone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种看不见的作用笼罩整个行星，于是这个词也用于比任何磁石都大得多的场。

senses.title: Storing data in magnetized material
senses.definition: using magnetized material to record and keep information
senses.definitionCN: 用被磁化的材料记录并保存信息
senses.example: The old magnetic tape still holds the studio recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 那卷旧磁带里还存着当年的录音。
senses.why: A magnet can fix a pattern in iron particles, and a fixed pattern can carry a signal, so magnetism became a way to write memory.
senses.whyCN: 磁体能在铁微粒里固定下一道图案，而固定图案可以承载信号，于是磁性成了写入记忆的手段。

senses.title: Having two opposite poles
senses.titleCN: 分南北极、同极相斥异极相吸
senses.definition: having north and south poles that attract and repel one another
senses.definitionCN: 具有南北两极，同极相斥、异极相吸
senses.example: Two magnetic poles of the same kind push each other away.
senses.exampleCN: 两个同类的磁极会把对方推开。
senses.why: The pull is never single: it always comes in a pair of opposite ends, which is why the adjective also describes polarity.
senses.whyCN: 这种拉力从不单独出现，总是成对的两端，因此这个词也用来描述极性。

senses.title: Charming a room
senses.definition: having a personality that draws people strongly and willingly
senses.definitionCN: 具有让人不由自主被吸引的个性
senses.example: Her magnetic presence made the whole room quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种有磁性的气场让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the stone's invisible pull: nothing is said or forced, yet attention turns toward the person.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了磁石看不见的拉力：没有言语也没有强迫，注意力却转向那个人。

senses.title: An abstract pull
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不可抗拒的吸引力
senses.definition: exerting an attraction so strong that it feels physical
senses.definitionCN: 施加一种强到近乎物理层面的吸引
senses.example: The magnetic appeal of the old city keeps artists returning.
senses.exampleCN: 老城那种不可抗拒的吸引力让艺术家一再回来。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the stone: what is attracted is no longer iron but a person, a memory or a whole crowd.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把磁石一般化：被吸引的不再是铁，而是人、记忆或一整群人。

intro.en: Magnetic goes back to the Greek name of a stone from Magnesia, through Latin magnes and the later Latin adjective magneticus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnetic 经拉丁 magnes 与晚期拉丁形容词 magneticus，上溯希腊语中一种来自马格尼西亚的石头之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos, 'the stone of Magnesia', named a naturally magnetized iron ore. The place-name explanation is generally accepted, but the origin of the place name itself is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 意为「马格尼西亚的石头」，指一种天然带磁性的铁矿石。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的，但地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and later formed the adjective magneticus from the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词，作 magnes，属格 magnetis；后来又用同一词干构成形容词 magneticus。

items.en: English magnet is recorded in the thirteenth century through Old French magnete, and the adjective magnetic follows in the sixteenth.
items.cn: 英语 magnet 在十三世纪经古法语 magnete 出现，形容词 magnetic 则到十六世纪才跟上。

items.en: From the sixteenth century magnetic described the invisible influence itself, and magnetic field became standard after Faraday's experiments in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，magnetic 开始描述那种看不见的作用本身；到十九世纪法拉第的实验之后，magnetic field 成为标准说法。

items.en: Animal magnetism, the theory Franz Mesmer promoted in the 1770s, supplied the metaphor of a person who draws others like iron to a lodestone.
items.cn: 梅斯默在十八世纪七十年代推崇的「动物磁力」理论，提供了「人像铁被磁石吸引」这一比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (place name and first record): the link to Magnesia is generally accepted, yet the origin of the place name and the exact earliest English citation of magnetic remain unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（地名与首见记录）：与马格尼西亚的联系一般认为是成立的，但地名的来源以及 magnetic 最早的确切英语书证仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same magnet stem, plus one look-alike from a different root; group two holds words for the pull itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 magnet 词干的词，另加一个形近却异源的词；第二组是表示「吸引力」本身的词。

entries.definition: The stone or device itself; magnetic is the adjective made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 磁石或磁体本身；magnetic 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The property or the science, not the object; the ending -ism marks a state or system.
entries.definitionCN: 指性质或学科，而不是物件；-ism 后缀标记状态或体系。

entries.definition: The black iron ore that can be magnetized; the ending -ite marks a mineral.
entries.definitionCN: 能被磁化的黑色铁矿石；-ite 后缀标记矿物。

entries.definition: A powerful person in business or industry, from Latin magnus 'great'; it shares spelling only, not ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 商业或工业界的权贵，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；只同拼写，并不同源。

entries.definition: Pleasing enough to draw interest, used of looks or offers; it carries no hint of a field.
entries.definitionCN: 足够讨喜而引来兴趣，多用于外貌或条件；不含磁场的意味。

entries.definition: Able to inspire followers through force of personality; narrower than magnetic and mainly about leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 靠人格力量鼓舞追随者；比 magnetic 窄，主要用于领袖。

entries.definition: Attractive in a way that promises pleasure or gain; it suggests enticement rather than natural pull.
entries.definitionCN: 以快乐或利益诱人的；偏「引诱」而非自然吸引。

entries.definition: So absorbing that attention cannot leave it; stronger and stranger than magnetic.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人到无法移开注意；比 magnetic 更强也更奇异。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stem, the real compounds and the real phrases of the magnet family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词干、真实的复合词，以及磁石词族里真实存在的搭配。

normal.en: The stem is the name of a stone from Magnesia, so magnet came before magnetism and magnetic.
normal.cn: 词干来自马格尼西亚的一种石头之名，因此先有 magnet，才有 magnetism 与 magnetic。

normal.en: The family runs magnet, magnetism, magnetize, magnetite, electromagnet and magnetometer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnet、magnetism、magnetize、magnetite、electromagnet 与 magnetometer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: magnetic field, magnetic pole, magnetic force, magnetic compass.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：磁场、磁极、磁力、磁罗盘。

normal.en: The same adjective serves the metaphor: a magnetic personality draws people the way a stone draws pins.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词也承担比喻：有魅力的个性吸人，正如磁石吸针。

normal.en: Electricity and magnetism sit side by side: electromagnet joins electro- to magnet.
normal.cn: 电与磁并肩而立：electromagnet 由 electro- 与 magnet 拼成。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible hand under the paper: the filings line up though nothing touches them.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下有一只无形的手：没有东西碰到铁屑，它们却排好了队。

abstract.en: Picture two ends that cannot be separated: cut the bar in half and each half still has a north and a south.
abstract.cn: 想象两个无法分开的端点：把磁条切成两半，每一半仍有南极和北极。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one speaker without being told to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人没有接到任何指令，却慢慢朝同一个演讲者靠过去。

examples.en: The magnetic strip on the card was worn, so the machine could not read it.
examples.cn: 卡片上的磁条磨损了，机器读不出来。

examples.en: Iron is strongly magnetic, while copper barely responds at all.
examples.cn: 铁有很强的磁性，而铜几乎毫无反应。

examples.en: The campaign gained magnetic force once the young mayor joined it.
examples.cn: 年轻市长加入之后，这场运动有了强大的吸引力。

dict_mnemonic.text: magnet（磁石）+ -ic（形容词后缀）——像磁石那样会吸 → 有磁性的；也有吸引力

root: 希腊语 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚的石头）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 拉丁形容词 magneticus → 英语 magnetic；地名来源一般认为是，地名本身来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a stone pulling iron, pass through field, machine and stored data, and end with the pull a person or a place exerts on a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一块吸铁的石头出发，经过磁场、机器与存储的数据，最后落到一个人或一个地方对人群的吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone moves iron across a sheet of paper without ever touching it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头隔着纸移动铁，却从不接触它。

branches.en: The stone and its poles: attraction and repulsion are two faces of one property.
branches.cn: 磁石与其两极：吸与斥是同一种性质的两张脸。

branches.en: From property to force: what the physicist measures is what the machine harnesses.
branches.cn: 从性质到力：物理学家测量的，正是机器所利用的。

branches.en: The planet itself as one huge magnet with a field around it.
branches.cn: 行星本身就是一块巨大的磁铁，外面罩着一层场。

branches.en: The pull fixed into matter as a pattern that can be read back.
branches.cn: 把拉力固定进物质，变成可以读回的图案。

branches.en: The same pull felt between people, or toward a place or an idea.
branches.cn: 同样的拉力发生在人与人之间，或指向一个地方、一个念头。

intro.en: Magnetic is an adjective built on the noun magnet with the Latin suffix -ic, so the whole family reads outward from the stone.
intro.cn: magnetic 是名词 magnet 加拉丁形容词后缀 -ic 构成，整个词族都可以从磁石向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes, genitive magnetis, came from Greek magnēs; New Latin added magnetismus for the property, and English built the rest on that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes（属格 magnetis）来自希腊 magnēs；新拉丁语又加 magnetismus 表示性质，英语其余词都建在这个词干上。

items.meaning: a stone or device that attracts iron
items.example: The magnet held the note to the steel door.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁把便条吸在钢门上。

items.meaning: of a magnet; able to attract
items.meaningCN: 磁的；有吸引力的（加形容词后缀，由物件转为性质）
items.example: The magnetic field bends the beam.
items.exampleCN: 磁场使电子束偏转。

items.meaning: the property of magnets; the science of it
items.meaningCN: 磁性；磁学（加状态后缀，由物件转为性质与学科）
items.example: Magnetism puzzled naturalists for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 磁性感住了博物学家好几个世纪。

items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加动词后缀，表示使成为）
items.example: The current magnetizes the iron core.
items.exampleCN: 电流使铁芯磁化。

items.meaning: the process or degree of becoming magnetic
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化程度（再加名词后缀，表示过程与结果）
items.example: Magnetization reverses as the current alternates.
items.exampleCN: 电流交变时，磁化方向随之反转。

items.meaning: the black iron ore that magnets occur in
items.meaningCN: 磁铁矿（加矿物后缀，由性质转到具体矿石）
items.example: Magnetite lies in bands along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁矿沿着山脊成带状分布。

items.meaning: a magnet worked by an electric coil
items.meaningCN: 电磁铁（由「电」与人造磁体复合，动力来源改变）
items.example: The electromagnet drops the load when switched off.
items.exampleCN: 断电时电磁铁把货物放下。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring magnetic strength
items.meaningCN: 磁强计（加测量器械后缀，由性质转为量具）
items.example: The survey used a magnetometer over the wreck.
items.exampleCN: 勘测时用磁强计扫过沉船。

items.meaningCN: 非磁性的（加否定前缀，性质被取消）
items.example: The case is made of nonmagnetic steel.
items.exampleCN: 外壳用的是非磁性钢。

latinEntries.meaning: the region that gave the stone its name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 给这种石头命名的那一地区

definition_zh: 磁性；磁学；磁力作用；吸引力，魅力
definition_en: the property of attracting iron, the science that studies it, or a strong power to attract people
core_image: 一块磁石周围看不见的场：铁屑一进入范围就自动转向，像被一条条虚线牵着
scene: 讲台上，老师把一块黑石放到铁屑上方，铁屑立刻立起来，像针刺一样指向同一个方向。Magnetism arranges the filings before anyone touches them.
sceneCN: 这里 magnetism 指「物质吸引铁的性质」（第 1 个义项：能吸铁并形成磁场）；句意为磁性在没人碰的情况下就把铁屑排好了方向。图中可辨识物件：黑石、铁屑、讲台、投影幕。

pos.zh: 磁性；磁力；磁学
吸引力；魅力（不可数）

forms.label: 名词（复数，罕用，指多种磁现象）

senses.title: The property of attracting iron
senses.definition: the property of a material that attracts iron and produces a field around it
senses.definitionCN: 物质吸引铁并在周围产生磁场的性质
senses.example: Magnetism makes the compass needle swing toward the north.
senses.exampleCN: 磁性让罗盘指针转向北方。
senses.why: The word names what the stone does, separated from the stone itself: a property rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是磁石所做的事，并与石头本身分开：它是一种性质，而不是一件东西。

senses.title: The branch of physics
senses.titleCN: 磁学：研究磁现象的学科
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies magnets, fields and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究磁体、磁场及其效应的物理分支
senses.example: She taught magnetism to first-year physics students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给物理系一年级学生讲授磁学。
senses.why: Once the property could be measured, it became a subject with laws, instruments and textbooks.
senses.whyCN: 当这种性质可以被测量，它就成了一门有定律、有仪器、有教科书的学科。

senses.title: Force around a magnet or coil
senses.titleCN: 磁力作用：磁体或线圈施加的力
senses.definition: the force that a magnet or a current-carrying coil exerts on nearby objects
senses.definitionCN: 磁体或通电线圈对附近物体施加的力
senses.example: The magnetism of the coil pulled the iron core inward.
senses.exampleCN: 线圈的磁力把铁芯往里吸。
senses.why: Property seen from the receiving side is force: the same thing that makes iron line up also pushes and pulls it.
senses.whyCN: 从受力的一方看，性质就是力：让铁排队的东西，同时也在推拉它。

senses.title: The link between current and magnet
senses.titleCN: 电磁：电流与磁的相互作用
senses.definition: the magnetic effect of an electric current and the electric effect of a changing magnet
senses.definitionCN: 电流产生的磁效应，以及变化磁场产生的电效应
senses.example: The discovery of magnetism around a live wire changed telegraph design.
senses.exampleCN: 带电导线周围存在磁效应这一发现，改变了电报的设计。
senses.why: A current behaves like a magnet, so the single word covers both sides of the link that later became electromagnetism.
senses.whyCN: 电流的行为就像一块磁铁，因此这同一个词覆盖了后来被称为电磁学那条联系的两端。

senses.title: The earth's pull
senses.titleCN: 地磁：地球与动物的导航依据
senses.definition: the natural magnetic influence of the earth that compasses and some animals use
senses.definitionCN: 地球天然产生的磁作用，罗盘与部分动物据此导航
senses.example: Pigeons appear to sense the earth's magnetism on long flights.
senses.exampleCN: 鸽子在长途飞行中似乎能感知地磁。
senses.why: The planet behaves like one enormous magnet, so the same word names the field that compasses and animals follow.
senses.whyCN: 行星的行为就像一块巨大的磁铁，因此同一个词也指罗盘与动物所依循的那个场。

senses.title: A magnetized state kept in metal
senses.titleCN: 剩磁：留在金属里的磁化状态
senses.definition: the degree to which a material has been magnetized and still holds a field
senses.definitionCN: 材料被磁化后仍保有磁场的程度
senses.example: Heating the hammer destroyed the magnetism stored in its head.
senses.exampleCN: 加热锤子毁掉了它头部存着的那点磁性。
senses.why: A property can be left behind in an object, so magnetism also names a stored condition rather than an active stone.
senses.whyCN: 性质可以残留在物体里，因此 magnetism 也指一种被储存下来的状态，而不是正在起作用的磁石。

senses.title: Personal charm
senses.titleCN: 个人魅力：吸引人的气质
senses.definition: a strong personal quality that draws other people
senses.definitionCN: 吸引他人的强烈个人气质
senses.example: Her magnetism filled the small lecture hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的魅力让那间小讲堂坐得满满当当。
senses.why: The old theory of animal magnetism treated personal influence as a fluid, and the figurative sense kept the idea of an invisible pull.
senses.whyCN: 旧的「动物磁力」理论把人的影响力当作一种流体，比喻义保留了「看不见的拉力」这一想法。

senses.title: The pull of a place or idea
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：地方或观念的吸引力
senses.definition: the power of a place, an idea or an activity to draw people toward it
senses.definitionCN: 地方、观念或活动把人吸引过去的力量
senses.example: The magnetism of the mountain towns keeps climbers coming back.
senses.exampleCN: 这些山间小镇的吸引力让登山者一再回来。
senses.why: The metaphor extends once more: now the field belongs to a landscape or a calling, not to a person.
senses.whyCN: 比喻再扩大一步：这一次场属于一片风景或一种召唤，而不属于某个人。

intro.en: Magnetism is a New Latin coinage built on the Greek and Latin name of the Magnesian stone. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnetism 是建立在该希腊、拉丁石名之上的新拉丁语造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos named the stone of Magnesia. The place-name origin is generally accepted, though the origin of the place name is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 指「马格尼西亚的石头」。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的，但地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and used it for both the ore and the force it showed.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该名词作 magnes，属格 magnetis，既指矿石，也指它显现出的那种作用。

items.en: Seventeenth-century scholars formed magnetismus to name the property itself rather than the stone that carries it.
items.cn: 十七世纪的学者造出 magnetismus，用来命名这种性质本身，而不是承载它的石头。

items.en: English adopted magnetism in the seventeenth century, first for the physical property and soon for the study of it.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收 magnetism，先用指物理性质，很快也指对它的研究。

items.en: Franz Mesmer's animal magnetism, promoted in the 1770s, treated personal influence as a fluid and gave English the sense of a charming, drawing power.
items.cn: 梅斯默在十八世纪七十年代推崇的「动物磁力」把人影响力当作流体，为英语留下了「迷人吸引力」这一义。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics made magnetism a measurable branch of study. The earliest English citation is dated only approximately, so the first record remains uncertain.
items.cn: 十九世纪物理学使 magnetism 成为可测量的学科。其最早的英语书证只能给出约略年代，因此首见记录属首见年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds relatives of the same magnet stem; group two holds nouns for the pull people feel.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 magnet 词干的亲属词；第二组是表示人所感受到的吸引力的名词。

entries.definition: The thing itself; magnetism is what it has or what it does.
entries.definitionCN: 物件本身；magnetism 是它所拥有或所施行的东西。

entries.definition: Describes something as magnet-like; magnetism is the noun behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容某物像磁石；magnetism 是它背后的名词。

entries.definition: A specific black mineral; it is one carrier of magnetism, not the property.
entries.definitionCN: 一种具体的黑色矿物；它是磁性的载体之一，而不是性质本身。

entries.definition: An industrial or business magnate, from Latin magnus 'great'; the resemblance is spelling only.
entries.definitionCN: 工业或商业巨头，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；相似只在拼写。

entries.definition: Any force or quality that draws things or people together; wider and plainer than magnetism.
entries.definitionCN: 任何把事物或人拉近的力或性质；比 magnetism 更宽也更平实。

entries.definition: A personal gift for inspiring devotion; it names the effect on people, not a physical field.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓舞他人忠诚的个人天赋；指对人的效果，而非物理场。

entries.definition: The quality of tempting someone toward something; it carries desire, which magnetism need not.
entries.definitionCN: 诱使人靠近的品质；带欲望色彩，而 magnetism 不一定有。

entries.definition: Everyday word for any drawing force, physical or social; magnetism is its technical and vivid version.
entries.definitionCN: 任何拉力的日常说法，物理或社会皆可；magnetism 是它技术化、形象化的版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stem, the real Latin coinage and the real compounds of the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词干、真实的新拉丁造词，以及词族中真实的复合词。

normal.en: The ending -ism turns a thing into a property or a system, so magnet plus -ism is magnetism.
normal.cn: -ism 把物件变成性质或体系，因此 magnet 加 -ism 就是 magnetism。

normal.en: The family runs magnet, magnetic, magnetize, magnetization, magnetite and electromagnetism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnet、magnetic、magnetize、magnetization、magnetite 与 electromagnetism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: animal magnetism, earth's magnetism, residual magnetism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：动物磁力、地磁、剩磁。

normal.en: The same noun serves the metaphor: the magnetism of a city or a singer.
normal.cn: 同一个名词也用于比喻：一座城市或一位歌手的吸引力。

normal.en: A current makes magnetism and a changing magnet makes current, which is why the pair is called electromagnetism.
normal.cn: 电流产生磁，变化的磁又产生电，因此这一对被称作电磁学。

abstract.en: Picture iron filings standing up like grass blades when the field arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象磁场到来时，铁屑像草叶一样立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hidden current under a table making every compass on it turn.
abstract.cn: 想象桌子底下有股隐藏的电流，让桌上所有罗盘一起偏转。

abstract.en: Picture a room that people enter for ten minutes and then cannot leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，人进去十分钟后就舍不得离开。

examples.en: Magnetism was studied long before anyone knew what an electron was.
examples.cn: 人们研究磁性时，还不知道电子是什么。

examples.en: The magnetism of the old harbour town draws painters every summer.
examples.cn: 这座老港镇的吸引力每年夏天都招来画家。

examples.en: Iron loses its magnetism when it is heated past a certain point.
examples.cn: 铁被加热到一定程度之后就会失去磁性。

dict_mnemonic.text: magnet（磁石）+ -ism（性质、体系）——磁石身上那种性质 → 磁性；研究它的学问 → 磁学

root: 希腊 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚石）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 新拉丁 magnetismus → 英语 magnetism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the property of a stone to the science of it, then to the force, the electric link, the earth's field, a stored state, and finally to the pull of a person or a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从石头的性质走到研究它的学科，再到力、与电的联系、地磁、残留状态，最后落到人或地方的吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible field around a stone that turns iron before anything touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：磁石周围有一层看不见的场，在没有任何接触之前就转动了铁。

branches.en: The property and its residue: what a material has, and what it keeps after the source is gone.
branches.cn: 性质与残留：材料拥有的，以及源头消失后仍留住的。

branches.en: The property made measurable, with laws and instruments of its own.
branches.cn: 性质变得可测量，有了自己的定律与仪器。

branches.en: Force around a coil, and the two-way link between current and magnet.
branches.cn: 线圈周围的力，以及电流与磁之间的双向联系。

branches.en: The whole planet as one field that birds and compasses read.
branches.cn: 整个行星成为一个场，鸟与罗盘都在读它。

branches.en: The field detached from metal and felt as charm or as the pull of a place.
branches.cn: 场脱离金属，被感受为魅力，或一个地方的吸引力。

intro.en: Magnetism is a noun formed from magnet with -ism, and the ending is the key to reading the family.
intro.cn: magnetism 是 magnet 加 -ism 构成的名词，这个后缀是读懂整个词族的钥匙。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes and Greek magnēs supply the stem; magnetismus is a New Latin noun, and English added the rest with native suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes 与希腊 magnēs 提供词干；magnetismus 是新拉丁名词，英语其余词则用本族后缀继续构造。

items.meaning: the stone or device that attracts iron
items.example: A magnet sat on the bench.
items.exampleCN: 工作台上放着一块磁铁。

items.meaning: the property of magnets; the science of it
items.meaningCN: 磁性；磁学（加状态后缀，由物件转为性质与学科）
items.example: Magnetism has its own units and laws.
items.exampleCN: 磁学有自己的单位与定律。

items.meaning: of magnets or of the force
items.meaningCN: 磁的；磁性的（加形容词后缀，由物件转为属性）
items.example: A magnetic field surrounds the coil.
items.exampleCN: 线圈周围有磁场。

items.meaning: to give magnetic properties to something
items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加使动后缀，性质被授予另一物体）
items.example: The pulse magnetizes the alloy.
items.exampleCN: 这一脉冲使合金磁化。

items.meaning: the act or degree of being magnetized
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化程度（再加过程后缀）
items.example: Magnetization falls as the metal heats.
items.exampleCN: 金属升温时磁化程度下降。

items.meaning: the linked science of electricity and magnetism
items.meaningCN: 电磁学（由「电」与磁性复合，两个领域合为一门）
items.example: Electromagnetism explains both motors and radios.
items.exampleCN: 电磁学同时解释电动机与无线电。

items.meaning: a device that measures magnetic strength
items.meaningCN: 磁强计（磁性加测量器械后缀，性质变成可读数）
items.example: The magnetometer read a sharp anomaly.
items.exampleCN: 磁强计读到一个明显的异常。

items.meaning: the field region around a planet
items.meaningCN: 磁层（磁性加球层后缀，场被扩展到行星尺度）
items.example: Charged particles gather in the magnetosphere.
items.exampleCN: 带电粒子聚集在磁层里。

items.meaning: a weak repulsion shown by some materials
items.meaningCN: 抗磁性（加「相对、反」前缀，吸引变成微弱排斥）
items.example: Water shows a faint diamagnetism.
items.exampleCN: 水表现出微弱的抗磁性。

latinEntries.meaning: the region linked to the stone's name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与这种石头之名相关的那一地区

definition_zh: 宏伟的；壮丽的；极好的；出色的；慷慨的；气魄宏大的
definition_en: impressively large and beautiful, excellent of its kind, generous on a grand scale, or noble in spirit
core_image: 一座巨大的穹顶压在石柱之上，让人抬头时不自觉放慢脚步
scene: 黄昏时分，游客站在广场尽头，抬头看那座穹顶，石阶上还留着白天的余温。The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
sceneCN: 这里 magnificent 是「宏伟的、壮丽的」（第 1 个义项：规模与形制令人震动）；句意为那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场托了起来。图中可辨识物件：石阶、穹顶、广场尽头的游客。

pos.zh: 宏伟的；壮丽的；极好的；慷慨的；气魄宏大的

derivatives.zh: 由 magnificent 加 -ence 构成，义为「宏伟；壮丽」
由 magnificent 加 -ly 构成，义为「宏伟地；极出色地」

senses.title: Impressively large and beautiful
senses.definition: so large and beautifully made or placed that it fills the eye and impresses the mind
senses.definitionCN: 规模巨大、形制或位置极美，足以占满视野并震动人心
senses.example: The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
senses.exampleCN: 那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场都托了起来。
senses.why: Latin magnificus joined magnus, great, to -ficus, making, so the word first praises what makes its surroundings look great.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magnificus 把意为「大」的 magnus 与意为「使……成」的 -ficus 拼在一起，所以这个词最初赞美的是让周围显得宏大的东西。

senses.title: Excellent of its kind
senses.definition: done or made to a very high standard, so that it stands out among others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 以极高水准完成或制成，在同类之中格外突出
senses.example: She gave a magnificent performance in the final act.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一幕献上了一场极为出色的演出。
senses.why: Greatness is measured by effect rather than by size, so a voice or a performance that overwhelms the audience earns the same word as a building does.
senses.whyCN: 宏大与否是看效果而不是看体积，所以一副压得住全场的好嗓子、一场压得住全场的演出，能和大建筑共用同一个词。

senses.title: Generous on a grand scale
senses.definition: giving freely and in large amounts, so that the gift itself feels splendid
senses.definitionCN: 毫不吝惜地大量给予，以至于所给之物本身就显得堂皇
senses.example: The old man made a magnificent gift to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人给村校捐了一份极为慷慨的礼物。
senses.why: Greatness turned outward becomes generosity, and a gift given without counting the cost looks as grand as any monument.
senses.whyCN: 宏大一旦朝外转，就成了慷慨；一份不计较代价送出的礼物，看上去和任何纪念碑一样气派。

senses.title: Noble and grand in spirit
senses.definition: showing a large, forgiving or courageous spirit in a moment of action
senses.definitionCN: 在行动的一刻显出宽厚、宽容或勇敢的气度
senses.example: He offered a magnificent gesture of forgiveness to the family who had wronged him.
senses.exampleCN: 他向那个曾亏待他的家庭做出了一个气魄宏大的宽恕姿态。
senses.why: If stone and sound can be magnificent, so can a choice, and the word extends from spectacle to the moral size of a person.
senses.whyCN: 既然石头与声音可以宏伟，一个选择也可以；这个词便从场面扩展到了人精神上的分量。

intro.en: Magnificent is built from two Latin pieces meaning great and making, and it reached English through French with the sense of grandeur already attached.
intro.cn: magnificent 由两个拉丁语成分拼成，分别意为「大」与「使……成」；它带着已有的「宏大」含义经法语进入英语。

items.en: Magnus was the ordinary Latin adjective for great in size, power or rank, and it stands behind a whole family of English words.
items.cn: magnus 是拉丁语中表示体积、力量或地位之「大」的普通形容词，一整族英语词都站在它背后。

items.en: The verb facere means to make or to do, and its combining form -ficus marks whatever produces or causes something.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为「做、造」，它的构词形式 -ficus 表示「产生、造成某物」。

items.en: Magnus plus -ficus gave magnificus, literally making great, and the word described things that enlarge the scene around them.
items.cn: magnus 加 -ficus 得到 magnificus，字面意为「使……变大」，用来形容把周围景象衬托得更大的事物。

items.en: The noun magnificentia named grandeur, and the comparative magnificentior supplied the form that passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 名词 magnificentia 指宏大、壮丽，比较级 magnificentior 提供了后来经法语进入英语的那个形式。

items.en: English borrowed magnificent in the fifteenth century and now applies it to buildings, performances, gifts and acts of spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 magnificent，如今把它用于建筑、演出、礼物，以及精神上的举动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin stem for great and making; the near group gathers adjectives that also praise scale, beauty or excellence.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「大」与「做」这两个词干上的同族词；近义组收同样赞美规模、美感或出色的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being grand and splendid.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟；壮丽；由 magnificent 加 -ence 构成。

entries.definition: In a grand or splendid manner.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟地；极出色地；由 magnificent 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To make something look larger, from the same Latin verb for making.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物看起来更大；与 magnificent 同出拉丁语中表示「做」的动词。

entries.definition: The great size or importance of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的巨大或重要程度；与 magnificent 共用拉丁语 magnus（大）。

entries.definition: Magnificent in appearance or very good indeed.
entries.definitionCN: 外观壮丽的；也确实非常好的。

entries.definition: Large and impressive in scale or style.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或气派上宏大而令人印象深刻的。

entries.definition: Having a dignified, royal beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 带有庄严、王者般的美感的。

entries.definition: Impressive because of size or presence.
entries.definitionCN: 因体积或气势而令人肃然起敬的。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin adjective for great to a Latin verb for making, and its family keeps returning to size, splendour and actions that enlarge the people who do them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「大」的形容词与表示「做」的动词拼在一起，它的同族词反复回到体积、壮丽，以及让做这件事的人显得更大的举动。

normal.en: Latin magnus means great, and -ficus comes from facere, to make, so magnificent is literally making great.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大」，-ficus 出自 facere（做），所以 magnificent 字面就是「使……宏大」。

normal.en: Magnificence adds -ence for the quality, and magnificently adds -ly for the manner of doing something.
normal.cn: magnificence 加 -ence 指性质，magnificently 加 -ly 指做事的方式。

normal.en: Magnify and magnitude share the same magnus stem, so the family keeps returning to size and greatness.
normal.cn: magnify 与 magnitude 共用 magnus 这个词干，所以这个词族一直回到体积与宏大。

normal.en: The word was borrowed through French in the fifteenth century, which is why it keeps the Latin -fic- shape.
normal.cn: 这个词在十五世纪经法语借入，所以至今保留拉丁语的 -fic- 形状。

normal.en: A magnificent view praises scale and beauty, while a magnificent gift praises generosity.
normal.cn: magnificent view 赞美规模与美，magnificent gift 赞美的则是慷慨。

abstract.en: Greatness that can be seen: the word always asks the eye to widen.
abstract.cn: 一种看得见的宏大：这个词总是要求人把眼界放宽。

abstract.en: A building and a kindness can both be magnificent, because both make the world around them look larger.
abstract.cn: 一座建筑与一份善意都可以是 magnificent，因为二者都让周围的世界显得更大。

abstract.en: The word joins great to make, a reminder that grandeur is often something done rather than owned.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「大」与「做」连在一起，提醒人：气派常常是做出来的，而不是拥有的。

examples.en: The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
examples.cn: 那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场都托了起来。

examples.en: She gave a magnificent performance in the final act.
examples.cn: 她在最后一幕献上了一场极为出色的演出。

examples.en: The old man made a magnificent gift to the village school.
examples.cn: 那位老人给村校捐了一份极为慷慨的礼物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马格尼菲森」——马戏团的大帐篷一拉开，全场都为它的宏伟惊叹；记住 magnificent 是宏伟的、极好的。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）+ -ficus（做、使……，源自 facere）→ magnificus（使显得宏大的）→ magnificentia 与比较级 magnificentior → 古法语 magnificent → 英语 magnificent。

sensesIntro.en: The core is greatness made visible; the senses then divide into imposing scale, excellent quality, lavish giving and a noble spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被看见的宏大」；义项由此分成震撼的规模、极高的水准、出手阔绰的给予，以及高尚的气度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast dome resting on stone columns, making every visitor slow down and look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座巨大的穹顶压在石柱之上，让每个来访者都放慢脚步抬头看。

branches.en: a dome lifting above the rooftops
branches.cn: 穹顶高过一片屋脊

branches.cn: 满堂观众爆出掌声

branches.en: a soloist holding the last note

intro.en: Two Latin stems, one for great and one for making, their Latin derivatives and two English endings carry magnificent from size to splendour and to generosity of spirit.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁词干，一个表示「大」，一个表示「做」，加上它们的拉丁派生词与两个英语词尾，把 magnificent 从体积带到壮丽，再带到精神上的慷慨。

latinIntro.en: Magnus, facere, magnificus and magnificentia are all recorded Latin words, and the English adjective descends from the same family through French.
latinIntro.cn: magnus、facere、magnificus 与 magnificentia 都是有记录的拉丁词，英语这个形容词经法语出自同一族。

definition_zh: 巨大；重要性；量值大小；震级；星等
definition_en: great size or importance, or the size of a quantity measured on a scale
core_image: 同一把刻度尺同时量山的高度与地震的力量，标记一路向上
scene: 地震台值班员盯着纸带上跳动的曲线，把刚测到的数字写进记录表。The seismologist logged a magnitude of six point two after the tremor.
sceneCN: 这里指「地震释放能量的大小等级」（第 4 个义项：按对数标尺给出的震级数值）；句意为地震学家在震动之后记录到六点二级。图中可辨识物件：记录纸带、曲线笔、值班台、墙上的地震仪。

pos.zh: 巨大；重要性；量值；震级；星等

senses.title: Great size or extent
senses.definition: the great size or extent of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物在体积或范围上的巨大
senses.example: The magnitude of the ice sheet surprised the survey team.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖的巨大规模让勘测队吃惊。
senses.why: Latin magnitudo named greatness in general, from magnus 'great' plus -tudo, a suffix for a state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 magnitudo 泛指「大」，由 magnus「大的」加表状态的后缀 -tudo 构成。

senses.title: Importance or seriousness
senses.definition: the importance or seriousness of an event or problem
senses.definitionCN: 事件或问题的重要程度与严重性
senses.example: Few understood the magnitude of the decision at the time.
senses.exampleCN: 当时很少有人明白这个决定有多重要。
senses.why: greatness of size turned into greatness of consequence, so a large event is one of large magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 规模之大转而指后果之大，因此重大的事件就是 magnitude 大的事件。

senses.title: Size of a measured quantity
senses.definition: the size of a quantity expressed as a number
senses.definitionCN: 以数字表示的量的大小
senses.example: The current rises in magnitude as the resistance falls.
senses.exampleCN: 电阻下降时，电流的量值上升。
senses.why: science needed a neutral word for how large a number is, whatever its unit.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性的词来指数字本身有多大，而不论其单位。

senses.title: Earthquake magnitude
senses.definition: a number on a logarithmic scale that expresses the energy released by an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 按对数标尺表示地震释放能量的数值
senses.example: The quake reached a magnitude of seven and toppled the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 地震达到七级，震倒了那道旧墙。
senses.why: the general sense of measured size was fixed to the seismic scale, where each step is a large jump in energy.
senses.whyCN: 「可量的大小」这一泛义被固定到地震标尺上，那里的每一级都代表能量的大幅跃升。

senses.title: Stellar magnitude
senses.definition: a number expressing the brightness of a star, with smaller numbers for brighter stars
senses.definitionCN: 表示恒星亮度的数值，星越亮数值越小
senses.example: The faint star has a magnitude of nine and needs a telescope.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗暗星是九等，需要望远镜才能看到。
senses.why: the ancient star catalogue ranked stars by brightness, and that ranking was later kept as a reversed numerical scale.
senses.whyCN: 古代星表按亮度给星排序，这一排序后来被保留为数值越小越亮的倒序标尺。

senses.title: Length of a vector
senses.definition: the length of a vector, considered apart from its direction
senses.definitionCN: 向量的长度，不考虑其方向
senses.example: The force has a magnitude of twelve newtons and points north.
senses.exampleCN: 这个力的大小是十二牛顿，方向朝北。
senses.why: mathematics separated how much from which way, and called the first part the magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 数学把「多大」与「朝哪」分开，并把前者称作 magnitude。

senses.title: Strength of a sound
senses.definition: the strength of a sound as measured in decibels
senses.definitionCN: 以分贝计量的声音强度
senses.example: The magnitude of the noise made sleep impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声的强度让人无法入睡。
senses.why: acoustics reused the measured-size sense for sound energy, again on a logarithmic scale.
senses.whyCN: 声学把「可量的规模」这一义用于声能，同样落在对数标尺上。

senses.title: Rank of importance
senses.definition: a rank or order of importance, as in a problem of the first magnitude
senses.definitionCN: 重要性的等级，如「头等重要的问题」
senses.example: They treated the leak as an issue of the first magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这次泄漏当作头等重要的问题。
senses.why: the star scale supplied a ready idiom in which rank is expressed by magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 星等标尺提供了一个现成的说法，用 magnitude 来表达等级。

intro.en: Magnitude comes from Latin magnitudo 'greatness, size', built on magnus 'great' and the state suffix -tudo. The word entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnitude 来自拉丁 magnitudo「巨大、规模」，由 magnus「大的」与表状态的后缀 -tudo 构成，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnus meant 'great, large, powerful'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the common link suggested to *meg- 'great' is a reconstructed root, not a proven source.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的、广阔的、有力的」。其更深来源不确定；常被提到的 *meg-「大」是重构词根，并非已证实的来源。

items.en: Magnus plus -tudo produced magnitudo 'greatness, size, extent', a third-declension noun.
items.cn: magnus 加 -tudo 构成 magnitudo「巨大、规模、范围」，是第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French magnitude carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first as a general term for greatness.
items.cn: 古法语 magnitude 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，最初泛指「巨大」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century magnitude was used for the size of a measurable quantity, especially in astronomy.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，magnitude 被用于可测量量的大小，尤其在天文学中。

items.en: The seismological sense dates from the twentieth century, when magnitude was fixed to a logarithmic energy scale.
items.cn: 地震学义始于二十世纪，当时 magnitude 被固定到对数能量标尺上。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): magnus has no established Indo-European ancestor, and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：magnus 没有已确定的印欧祖先，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root that look alike but mean different things; group two holds near-meaning size words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、形近而义异的词；第二组是语义相近的「大小」词。

entries.definition: From magnus plus -ficare 'to make': to make something appear larger, not to be large itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 magnus 加 -ficare「使」构成：使某物看起来更大，而不是自身巨大。

entries.definition: Magnus plus -ficent 'doing': splendid in appearance, close to grand rather than to measurable size.
entries.definitionCN: magnus 加 -ficent「做」：外观壮丽，接近「宏伟」，而非可测的规模。

entries.definition: Magnus plus animus 'mind': great-souled, generous, with nothing to do with physical size.
entries.definitionCN: magnus 加 animus「心」：心胸宏大的、宽厚的，与物理大小无关。

entries.definition: A graded set of numbers for brightness or energy; the compound names the instrument, while magnitude names the number.
entries.definitionCN: 表示亮度或能量的分级数值体系；复合词指这套标尺，而 magnitude 指其中的数值。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for how large a thing is; magnitude is its formal and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体有多大的日常词；magnitude 是其正式、技术化的对应词。

entries.definition: The degree to which something covers an area or reaches a limit, stressing spread rather than bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 某物覆盖面积或达到界限的程度，强调铺展而非体积。

entries.definition: The level at which something operates, as on a scale from small to large; magnitude is the reading on that scale.
entries.definitionCN: 事物运作的相对层级，如由小到大的标尺；magnitude 是标尺上的读数。

entries.definition: The harshness or seriousness of something bad; it adds the idea of harm that magnitude alone does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 坏事之严酷或严重；多了「造成伤害」的意思，而 magnitude 本身不含此意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphemes and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语素与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: magnus 'great' plus -tudo 'state' gives 'state of being great'.
normal.cn: magnus「大」加 -tudo「状态」即「大的状态」。

normal.en: Order of magnitude marks a jump of about ten times.
normal.cn: 数量级标记约十倍的跃升。

normal.en: Earthquake magnitude and stellar magnitude are both logarithmic scales.
normal.cn: 震级与星等都是对数标尺。

normal.en: Of the first magnitude means of the highest rank.
normal.cn: 头等重要的，即最高等级。

normal.en: The family runs magnitude, magnify, magnificent, magnification, magnanimous.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnitude、magnify、magnificent、magnification、magnanimous。

abstract.en: Picture one ruler long enough to measure both a mountain and a quake.
abstract.cn: 想象一把足够长的尺，既能量山，也能量地震。

abstract.en: Picture a star chart where the brightest star is given the smallest number.
abstract.cn: 想象一张星图，最亮的星反倒标着最小的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that grows until nobody can ignore its size.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻越滚越大，大到没人能忽视。

examples.en: Nobody grasped the magnitude of the loss until the accounts were closed.
examples.cn: 直到账目结清，人们才明白损失有多大。

examples.en: Each step on the magnitude scale means roughly thirty times more energy.
examples.cn: 震级标尺上的每一级大约意味着三十倍的能量。

examples.en: The magnitude of the vector is independent of its direction.
examples.cn: 向量的大小与其方向无关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「magni（大）+ tude（状态）」——大的状态就是「巨大、规模、量值」

root: 拉丁 magnus「大的」+ -tudo（表状态）→ magnitudo「巨大、规模」，经法语 magnitude 进入英语；magnus 更深来源不确定，*meg- 一说是重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much: bulk, consequence, number, seismic energy, starlight, vector length, sound and rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「有多大」：体积、后果、数值、地震能量、星光、向量长度、声音与等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single ruler marked from small to great, laid first against a mountain and then against a quake.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把由小到大的刻度尺，先量山，再量地震。

branches.en: SIZE AND WEIGHT: what is physically large becomes socially serious.
branches.cn: 体积与分量：物理上的大转化为社会意义上的重。

branches.cn: 地震标尺：这个数被固定到对数能量阶梯上。

intro.en: Magnitude is one Latin root plus one state suffix, and that root also builds several common English words.
intro.cn: magnitude 是一个拉丁词根加一个状态后缀，这个词根还构成若干常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus 'great' gives magnitude, magnify, magnificent and magnanimous; -tudo marks a state or quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnus「大」衍生 magnitude、magnify、magnificent 与 magnanimous；-tudo 标记状态或性质。

items.example: Magnus is the root behind the whole family.

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a noun of state.

items.example: The magnitude of the task was clear.

items.example: She was magnanimous in victory.

definition_zh: 主要地；首要地；大部分地；大体上
definition_en: chiefly, above all; for the most part
core_image: 一屋子的人里，绝大多数都举着同一种颜色的旗子
scene: 散场后，清洁工推着车穿过空荡的展厅，地上留下的东西并不多。The mess left behind was mainly paper cups and torn programmes.
sceneCN: 这里表示「大部分是」（第 2 个义项：大部分地）；句意为留下的垃圾主要是纸杯和撕破的节目单。

pos.zh: 主要地；首要地；大部分地

derivatives.zh: mainly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词与名词，义为「主要的；主管道」
由 main 与 stream 复合，义为「主流」

senses.title: Above all; chiefly
senses.definition: more than anything else, when the point is what matters most
senses.definitionCN: 在强调最重要的原因或因素时，表示「首要地、主要地」
senses.example: The delay was mainly caused by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 延误主要是风暴造成的。
senses.why: Main means chief, and -ly turns that judgement into an adverb: mainly marks the factor that outweighs the rest.
senses.whyCN: main 意为首要的，-ly 把这个判断变成副词：mainly 标出压过其余因素的那一个。

senses.title: For the most part
senses.definition: in most cases or to most of a group, when the point is quantity or proportion
senses.definitionCN: 在强调数量或比例时，表示「大部分、多数情况下」
senses.example: The audience was mainly students from nearby schools.
senses.exampleCN: 观众大部分是附近学校的学生。
senses.why: The same adverb can measure a group instead of ranking a cause, so mainly also means that most members share the trait being named.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词也可以衡量一个群体，而不是给原因排序，所以 mainly 还表示多数成员都具有所说的特征。

intro.en: Mainly is the adjective main fitted with the old adverb suffix -ly, and main itself goes back to a Germanic noun for strength.
intro.cn: mainly 是形容词 main 加上古老的副词后缀 -ly 构成，而 main 本身可追溯到日耳曼语表示力量的名词。

items.en: The base is mægen, a noun for strength or force.
items.cn: 基础词是 mægen，一个表示力量或威力的名词。

items.en: The reconstructed *maginam is the common Germanic source of mægen and of might.
items.cn: 重构形式 *maginam 是 mægen 与 might 共同的日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English main took the sense chief or principal from that root.
items.cn: 中古英语 main 从这一词根取得「首要、主要」的意思。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly, from Old English -līce, was added to main to make mainly.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 源自古英语 -līce，加在 main 后构成 mainly。

items.en: Modern English uses mainly for both the leading cause and the largest share of a group.
items.cn: 现代英语里 mainly 既指首要原因，也指群体中的最大部分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on main; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of majority and chief importance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 main 构成的形式；近义组收表示多数与首要地位的副词。

entries.definition: Chief or principal; also a principal pipe or supply.
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；也指主管道或公共供应。

entries.definition: The principal land mass, as opposed to islands.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于岛屿而言的主要陆地；大陆。

entries.definition: Ideas or practices accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被多数人接受的思想或做法；主流。

entries.definition: The chief support of a system or group.
entries.definitionCN: 系统或群体的主要支柱。

entries.definition: In most cases or to the greatest degree.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下；大部分地。

entries.definition: Above all; mainly.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地；主要地。

entries.definition: To a great extent; mostly.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上；大部分。

entries.definition: Mainly; in the majority.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；占多数地。

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds -ly to a word for strength and chief weight, so it can rank a cause or measure a majority.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词把 -ly 加在表示力量与首要分量的词后，因此既能给原因排序，也能衡量多数。

normal.en: Mainly is main plus -ly, so the adverb keeps the idea of ranking: one thing outranks the rest.
normal.cn: mainly 是 main 加 -ly，所以这个副词保留了排序的意思：某样东西压过其余。

normal.en: The -ly ending comes from Old English -līce, which turned a quality into a manner of acting.
normal.cn: -ly 词尾来自古英语 -līce，把某种性质变成行事的方式。

normal.en: When mainly points at a cause, it works like chiefly; when it points at a crowd, it works like mostly.
normal.cn: 当 mainly 指向原因时，它相当于 chiefly；当它指向一群人时，它相当于 mostly。

normal.en: The word is a judgement about weight, so mainly does not mean only; other factors can still be present.
normal.cn: 这个词是对分量的判断，所以 mainly 不等于 only，其他因素仍可能存在。

normal.en: Mainly because and mainly due to are the two phrases that show the adverb ranking a reason.
normal.cn: mainly because 与 mainly due to 是展示这个副词给原因排序的两个短语。

abstract.en: A hall where nearly everyone holds the same colour of flag: the crowd shows what mainly means.
abstract.cn: 满厅几乎人人举着同一种颜色的旗子：人群本身就展示了 mainly 的意思。

abstract.en: To say what mainly caused something is to put one weight on the scale and let the others stay lighter.
abstract.cn: 说出某件事主要因何而起，就是在一杆秤上放一个更重的砝码，让其余都轻一些。

abstract.en: Ranking and proportion are two faces of one adverb, both asking which part deserves the emphasis.
abstract.cn: 排序与比例是同一个副词的两张脸，两者都在问哪一部分值得强调。

examples.en: The delay was mainly caused by the storm.
examples.cn: 延误主要是风暴造成的。

examples.en: The audience was mainly students from nearby schools.
examples.cn: 观众大部分是附近学校的学生。

examples.en: The mess left behind was mainly paper cups and torn programmes.
examples.cn: 留下的垃圾主要是纸杯和撕破的节目单。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is ranking by weight; it splits into the leading cause and the largest share of a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是按分量排序；义项分成首要原因与群体中的最大部分。

branches.cn: 用一个副词既给原因排序，也数出多数
